utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. Very good morning to everybody. May we hear the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. This is Case Number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Nicholas Koumjian with Ruth Karper for the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Branko Lukic and John Ostojic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning, and thank you. Before we start, first, my apologies that we start belated. Something was to be discussed before we were able to start today's hearing. Let me turn to some specific issues that were found out during the weekend. First, we have this large document on the authorship of decisions, orders, conclusions, and other document. And I congratulate for the inventive and innovative OTP. I have never seen until now the word "gazetted" and so on, but probably it may be a new word. I haven't heard this word before. It is interesting to see. But we have a real problem with this analysis because there are numerous documents mentioned that have not yet been tendered, or some of them have even not yet a 65 ter number. I think we can't work on this basis before the documents are tendered by the OTP, and we would kindly request the OTP to present for this purpose a List 7 of documents. You can find it immediately on the first column of your overview. Then it was - and I don't think whether the parties have the same impression - a little bit difficult to work with and even to read the handwriting expertise because reference it made to ERN numbers and not to the documents, not to the exhibit numbers. It would be helpful if this could be added, or even better, a compilation of the documents mentioned in this expertise could be added separately for a better understanding of the expertise as such, and for an easier discussion of the documents when we have the expert before us. Let's come one step further to witnesses. We discussed the envisaged schedule of the OTP during the 65 ter conference last Thursday. It remained open until now whether or not to call ex officio the bishop of Banja Luka. The Defence has asked for the possibility to discuss this issue with Dr. Stakic. And it remains the question whether or not the Defence is contesting the content of this. If so, it would be necessary to call the bishop. May we hear some explanations by the Defence as regards this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. The Defence, and we would like to thank the Court for granting us addition time in order to review and make an analysis with our client in connection with the bishop's letter dated August 11th of 1992. Our position is as follows: Without waiving our right to remain silent, the Defence in a continuing effort to cooperate with the Court and the Tribunal do not contest the contents of the letter from the bishop with the exception of the fact that the OTP may, and the Court may, respectfully, make an inference with respect to whether or not Dr. Stakic received the letter dated August 11th, 1992. The Defence's position specifically in regard to this issue is that we deny that the letter was received by Dr. Stakic; and further deny that the contents described by the honourable bishop following the August 4th, 1992 meeting were known by Dr. Stakic. Namely, if the Court remembers, and I can appreciate the Court's preliminary comments singularly referencing content, but there are three specific dates in the letter and conversations with other individuals. It's our position, quite frankly, that the first portion of that letter we do not contest, and we believe it was the Court's request on that portion of the letter that we will not contest. However, with respect to the discussions subsequent to August 11th or information that the bishop may have learned after the August 4th, 1992, meeting, as well as receipt of the documents, we do expressly deny and would object to, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. May we hear some observations as regards this by the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would just point out that in many jurisdictions, there's a presumption. It's just based upon reasonableness that a letter sent was received. I don't expect that the sender would necessarily be able to testify whether or not a letter was received, simply that it was sent. Other than that, I have no further comments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then, also under the headline "witnesses" and -- sorry. Also under the headline "witnesses and right to be heard," I have to address the following issue: During the Prosecutor's case, the authenticity of minutes taken is in nearly all of the cases contested by the Defence. Sometimes we find attached a name of a rapporteur or a person having drafted or at least then later signed these minutes not signed by Dr. Stakic. As long as the authenticity is contested, we are afraid it is necessary to exhaust all possible means, and this would mean to hear the person or the persons mentioned at the end of those minutes. Therefore, my question goes to, first, the OTP: Is it the intention to call this rapporteur or rapporteurs?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Is it the intention of the Defence to present these rapporteurs during the Defences case? We don't want to destroy the Defence case.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The Defence, Your Honour, is still contemplating whether we will call such witnesses in our case, in our response, or Defence case. We will have to evaluate that after the 98 bis motions and after the conclusion of the case in chief by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Therefore, we have to deliberate on this, and we have to decide on this. But the parties should not be surprised if they find a document calling this rapporteur or the rapporteurs during the Prosecutor's case. I think the attempt is mandatory. Let me finally go to the schedule: We anticipated that Monday 23 and Wednesday 25 should be reserved for deliberations. And as we discussed it, the Monday should be reserved for deliberations on facts; Wednesday for deliberations on legal aspects. In anticipation of these deliberations, it would be helpful if we could receive, if possible, in writing those parts of the indictment where it is the intention of the Office of the Prosecutor to drop certain factual allegations, say, just to quote out of the blue, that the OTP is no longer of the opinion that for what reasons ever, for example, that the witness wasn't able to come, they themselves believe that there's no evidence, for example, that one mosque was destroyed. This would facilitate, and this is the purpose of this entire exercise, facilitate and abbreviate the notions and the scope of what has to be discussed during the -- for the purpose of the 98 bis motion. As then regards the deliberations on the legal aspects, no doubt that we then at the end of the Prosecutor's case expect a clarification what has to be the Defence case. We'll say that we will no longer accept that we have parallelly allegations that Dr. Stakic ordered, incited, committed, aided and abetted an offence. It should be and it has to be for the purpose of a fair trial clear, at least at that point in time, what are the remaining charges after the OTP has had the opportunity to present all the evidence available. Finally, and you never should lose the hope, one aspect of these deliberations could be, of course, that we could come - and once again, try to come to an agreement between the parties. I think under the impression of that what we have heard since April 16, it shouldn't be too difficult to come to such an agreement. I know there's a gap between the expectations of the parties, but I don't believe that this is a gap that couldn't be bridged. And it's necessary that if possible this gap has to be bridged because also in this case, but this is not the first and not the most important reason, coefficiency aspects have to play a role. Furthermore, it is of incredible value that we would have the chance to come to a decision based on agreement because opposed to ordinary courts, we have the additional mandate to maintain peace and to bring people living in the area of Former Yugoslavia together again. And therefore, an agreement as such has an incredible value, and no doubt that this would have to be taken into account in a possible outcome of this case. If it would be possible that Dr. Stakic himself would feel able to give us an insight on his own state of mind, his own intentions, his own way to that what he exercised in the many-fold capacities we learned during the time since April 16, it would be helpful. No doubt it is correct what one of Defence counsel said during the 65 ter meeting: "Sometimes it is indeed not in favour of the client to give the recommendation to address the Court." But on the other hand, it should be considered, and after all that what I have heard and seen here in the courtroom as regards the activities of Dr. Stakic and his being impressed by that what he heard from witnesses, I think it would be appropriate, and it could be indeed helpful, if we could hear how it came to this development from a physician going into politics and then being faced, to put it very neutral, with results of politics dominant at that time in the area, politics from -- emanating from at least two different sides. We all know that we can't apply the tu quoque principle here. And we have to under the question before us whether or not there's an individual responsibility of Dr. Stakic. But for this purpose, and also for the purpose to learn more of his personal development about the use, about the background of his growing up, about his political development, how the entire story ended. Why, for example, then later on he left Prijedor. All this would be of extreme importance for this Tribunal. So therefore, these words cannot have more than an appellate function. But we should take into account that it would be extremely high value that we hear from an accused that he no longer maintains a possible formal role and that let's for a moment leave aside the question of responsibility, regrets, what was the outcome of the politics at that time in the area of Former Yugoslavia. This, no doubt, could bring us closer to the expectations of the Defence as regards the outcome of the case. And no doubt, also the Office of the Prosecutor, to a certain extent, has to come down to earth as regards the possible outcome of the case. We have -- the Bench has several times discussed the case as it stands now. And we can anticipate what will be the development during the next four weeks. Based on this, and knowing about the gap to be bridged, I think it can and it must be possible to limit this case to what it is on the mere - and this is important enough - responsibility of Dr. Stakic. I know, having been a Prosecutor myself for more than ten years how difficult it is when you have once started a case against three persons, and now one person is remaining, that you can't possibly not find out the persons who were really responsible on the level of Prijedor, I must emphasise, for that what happened deplorably at that time. It can't be true that in the beginning, there were three accused, and now one has to pay for the three of them. So therefore, for the last time, once again, being aware that this has only an appellate function, I would ask the parties to try to come together and to envisage that we try on the basis of the deliberations of 23 and 25 September once again - and I really believe this is the last occasion then - to come to an agreement as foreseen in our rules on procedure and evidence. I really believe it's necessary because I personally see a good chance to come to such an agreement. I don't expect any comments on this right now. Please, bear it in mind. And let us now turn, once again, down to earth to a more administrative matters. Is there anything to add to that what we discussed during the 65 ter meeting or anything -- any changes in the schedule of the OTP for the next four weeks already foreseeable now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: From the Defence, any problems with lists expected from -- to be prepared by Mr. Inayat or other issues?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, quite frankly, I do have a comment on it, and I was hoping to clarify the issue with Mr. Inayat this morning. I do believe that there are -- is a list that still is missing in connection with the documents that are in the possession of the OTP. However, when reviewing over this weekend the actual direct and cross-examination, it may be that our questions at that time were overly broad and not specific enough, and therefore there might be a discrepancy as to which lists we find necessary and relevant for purposes of authenticating certain documents as well as determining whether or not certain documents are relevant, much less credible. I can share with the Court what it is specifically that I'm inquiring about. We raised it in the 65 ter conference, and that would be an index of the list of documents, if I may, that were prepared and submitted to the OTP by the agency called the agency for identification and documentation, namely with the acronym AID which was part and parcel a unit from the federal government of Bosnia-Herzegovina previously identified as being their, I think, secret service centre. It's those documents, Your Honour, we specifically would contest are relevant since many of the documents that the OTP has submitted and expect the Court to make analysis from and rely upon, I think the sourcing are critically relevant and valuable. And we have a position in connection with those sources that we think can enlighten the Court and at least give it some guidance respectfully in connection with the weight that those documents may be given. Again, I accept the Court has accepted and admitted those documents. But when we address the weight, we feel that depending on who the source is and how that may have reached the hands of the OTP, the timing, et cetera, it may be of some interest. So we don't have that list in particular. But the other ones we have, and unfortunately I read through most of those 2.000 pages of indexes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think the remaining issue can be discussed in the presence and of course with Witness Inayat immediately. Are there other remaining issues to be prepared possibly with the assistance of the Bench not related to Mr. Inayat?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I mentioned to my learned friend just a couple of things that are outstanding, although it's not a complaint just a matter of follow-up. Perhaps we should list it on the record just to be efficient. We have not yet received the CV or a curriculum vitae of a couple of their proposed witnesses, namely the military expert as well as the linguistics individual who is testifying. In addition, we have not yet received the report, the military analytical report in the language in which the accused can understand and assist in preparation of his Defence. We have to date not received the updated or supplemental report from Dr. Eva Tabeau. With the exception of those three items, the CV, the reports in the language in which the accused can understand, the military report, the supplemental report from the demographer, I don't think we have any other comments. In addition to that, the report from the linguistics analyst in either English or in B/C/S has not been tendered to date. And we know it's in draft, and the linguist was out of town last week, I believe. So we hope to get that at least several days before that person would be called to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this. Observations by the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just to go through the outstanding matters to be provided to the Defence, the translation of the military report is finished and will be provided at the break. It was finished over the weekend. The CVs -- both of those individuals were out of town last week, and I've asked them both to provide the CVs. I may have to get together with counsel and maybe the Court on one of them. There may be an issue we have to raise in private session. In regards to the report of the linguist or document analyst I would call him, again, he's out -- he was out of town last week. I'm not sure if he's back. I do have some questions I wanted to go over with him before we submitted his draft or before it's finalised and he may have made some changes in the meantime. If he's not back today, then I'll simply provide the draft, even though it will be changed, to the Defence so they can start reading it. As for Ms. Tabeau's report on Prijedor, that will be provided on -- she said that would be finished by next Monday. I will also inform the Court and counsel something I found out late Friday. There's a good chance that we will get today an updated version, an electronic version, of the Prijedor book of missing persons that apparently all the data has been inputted and we are trying to arrange to be shipped here as soon as possible. I do have one other question regarding the Court's earlier remarks, and a clarification that I would request. When the Court talks about deliberations, are those arguments? I'm not quite sure. Are we going to all be sitting in Court discussing this, or is there deliberations by the Bench without the parties amongst yourselves? I'm confused about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It's the attempt to come in public session to some kind of agreement between the parties in the presence of the Court with some hopefully assistance of the Court. The Bench will make up -- we will make up our minds until then, and probably we can give some guidance and indicate where we see problems and where we don't see problems. May I ask, does the Office of the Prosecutor share our view that those documents mentioned here in this huge document should be tendered and will be tendered?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I don't think it would terribly hurt other than we would have a lot more documents. Let me explain, some of those have been admitted, but when this prepared apparently the preparer did not have the S numbers. Particularly those would be 65 ter numbers 43, which is 192; 45 as 193; 48 as 194; and 49 as 195. Many of the others are duplicates or are orders on matters that we didn't find particularly probative such as establishing branch offices in Ljubija and other places. But perhaps for the clarity of both this report -- we could either take it off this report, but perhaps for the clarity of having all the documents with the signature or the name of Dr. Stakic, and also to probably -- some of these may be referred to in Mr. Corin, the linguist's report, it would be better to add to this another list. In regards to list 7, in other words the documents not on the first six lists, we have a working list. Of course that will not be complete probably until the trial -- or at least there -- all the documents may not be in until September the 18th or whenever we finish. Mr. Inayat, I will ask him about that today, but he will be providing the sourcing of all those documents which he already has that information. It simply will be inputted by Ms. Karper into the report based on Mr. Inayat's contributions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No doubt that some of the documents mentioned as such based on their content have no --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Some were duplicates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: -- are not that important probative value. But I think such an expertise cannot be based on documents not yet tendered or, as I mentioned, please find it on page 5, even not yet being in the possession of the Bench because not having a 65 ter number. So I think it's really necessary even taking into account the interest of the first, that we have to have all these documents available for a better discussion and understanding of this entire document. Therefore, we would be grateful if you could provide us with such additional documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I think that actually is the item -- the item Your Honour referred to number -- I believe that item that had no 65 ter number in the chart should have the 65 ter number 99. I believe it's part of gazette number 2. But we'll complete the chart and make sure that any exhibit, as Your Honour requested, that is not yet in evidence is added to list 7 or 8, wherever we are at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. I think it's now enough with initial remarks. I can't see any obstacles for starting now with Witness Inayat. It's the second testimony of Mr. Inayat. And may the usher please bring in Witness Inayat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Inayat. As to the fact that this is a new testimony, and your second testimony in the same case, I would ask you once again to give us the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Please, be seated. And may the examination-in-chief start.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Before I begin, I'd like to distribute lists 4, 5, and 6, and have one copy be given to the witness. I would also ask that they be given exhibit numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The next one will be S?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: S278, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: S278, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I believe the Defence already has the lists. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence as S278.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: So will that be all three lists, Your Honour, are 278?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So for the record, we have now been presented. List 4 will be S -- the new list 4 will be S278. List 5, 279. List 6, 280. Examined by Mr. Koumjian: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Inayat, you have in front of you S278, 279, and 280, lists 4, 5, and 6 respectively. These indicate documents listed by the 65 ter number, and where they have it by an S number, the documents described and the ERN numbers in both English and B/C/S provided and the last column indicates sources. Did you contribute to the preparation of these documents?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Specifically, did you provide the information that is in the far right column, "sources"?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you do this in the same manner that you did for lists 1, 2, and 3 that you testified about previously?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Inayat, the Court has noticed instances where the OTP has presented multiple copies of documents. Can you tell us first of all how did you handle the situation regarding your sourcing when documents were found in more than one location?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: While I was trying to find the sources for these documents, it so happened that I came across copies which had come to us from duplicate sources or sometimes even three or four sources. One of the primary source of these documents was the seizure that took place in Prijedor or also in Banja Luka, but in later years, we were also given or provided with similar copies from the local authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me stop there. In that situation where you received the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. documents from different sources, would the document, each copy, have a separate ERN number?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the charts for lists 4, 5, and 6 where we have an ERN number and then the source, does that source indicate for each ERN number, in other words, where it came from? Does that column sourcing indicate for each ERN number where we obtained -- the OTP obtained the document with that specific ERN number?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: There are several instances -- I don't know if there's a particular instance in these three documents, but there are several instances when I was doing the sourcing that I did mention that in the source column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For example, let's look at list 5, 65 ter number 43, the third one on the list.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This indicates -- and we have two different -- in the sourcing column, we have different ERN numbers. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: What this particular example means is that in fact it's the same document from the Prijedor seizure, but 00633787 means that before it was sent for stamping to the evidence unit --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down. Please repeat.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Example 43, 65 ter number 43, there are two ERN numbers mentioned in the B/C/S ERN. In fact, it's the same document. What happened was that before the collection was handed over to the evidence unit, when they stamped P007162, before this, the team had reviewed this particular document for the Kovacevic trial. And they had taken this document out and given it to the evidence unit which at that time in early 1998 gave the number 00633787. So this is not the example. It's not the right example here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it indicate that the first one, the ERN numbering 3787 was seized from the police station, and the second one, 7162, was seized from the Municipal Assembly building?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I apologise. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. President and witness, please, could you slow down and repeat all these numbers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: If we could just pause between the question and answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I would like to apologise. You're right. 00633787 was seized from the police station, and this similar document was also seized from the Municipal Assembly building. I'm sorry, that is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Inayat, were there instances when you went into a file in one location where the same document appeared more than once in that location or in a particular file?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: This is true. As I was explaining this a little earlier that one particular document may have come from different sources, and I have confirmed this several times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, for example, were there occasions when you went to the Municipal Assembly building and in one folder the same document appeared, in other words, the document and copies of the same document appeared in the same folder?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I wouldn't like to make a comment without having reviewed a particular example. But it is possible, as I said, that the same document may have come from the same location a number of times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you found that the same document, let's say a two-page document, appeared with the ERN numbers in sequence, in other words, ending 1, 2, 3, 4, would that indicate to you that the two documents, the two copies of the two-page document were found together in one location?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I just ask --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, if I can just...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'm trying to shorten things a bit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Inayat, have you actually done the sourcing for the entire 65 ter list?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I did this several months ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be correct if in the future in this case we present lists, further lists, lists 7 or 8 with a sourcing column, would you be the person that provides the information for that sourcing?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: My first question to the OTP is: Shouldn't the question about the further development of those documents seized during the arrest of Dr. Stakic should also form part of the examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just to clarify, the documents that Your Honour is speaking of are not the items in evidence. They are the documents that are actually seized and were returned to the Detention Unit. I don't want to speak in front of the witness in too much detail. What we have in evidence right now are the copies. But to make the picture complete, could we have S235. S235, do we have a copy?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Inayat, as the team leader for Team 1, were you the team leader at the time that Mr. Stakic was arrested?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after Mr. Stakic was arrested, did you speak to a Mr. O'Donnell?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. O'Donnell I believe a couple of days after the arrest came to my office and I spoke to him about the arrest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Inayat, have you seen a note by Mr. O'Donnell regarding what he did with certain documents that he obtained during -- when he arrested Mr. Stakic or took custody of him and brought him to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen that document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you have a recollection at all of receiving the documents from Mr. O'Donnell after Mr. Inayat -- excuse me, Dr. Stakic was arrested?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes. My recollection is that Mr. O'Donnell came to my office and showed me certain -- a certain material that appeared to me to be something of --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Could I look at the items first.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: The material that Mr. O'Donnell showed me, it appeared to be something like a private documentation, and I believe there were some keys. So I remember having seen those.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, what would your procedure be when you receive documents such as that were seized during the arrest of an individual?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: In a couple of previous examples when --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me interrupt if I may, Your Honour, with all due respect to the witness. I'd like to object to the question. I think it's improper. Counsel was trying to impute to this witness and to this Court that someone who gave them documents, and we are taking a completely different position on that. It wasn't documents received. We say that they were - as our briefs have indicated - documents that were improperly and illegally confiscated from the accused. So it's not a question of receiving, and I don't know if it may make a difference to a criminal investigator. I would hope that it does, but to that extent I object to the form of the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Dismissed because the question was clearly related to the handing over from Mr. O'Donnell to Mr. Inayat. And therefore, the word "receive" is more than appropriate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In any event, let me re-ask the question. Mr. Inayat, do you know or have you done any investigation to determine or to refresh your recollection what you did with the items you received from Mr. O'Donnell that were taken during the arrest and transfer of Dr. Stakic?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Like I was saying, in a couple of previous cases when people were brought here, I went through the personal items that were on these persons. And I had those returned, if they weren't relevant to the investigation. In the case of Mr. Stakic when Mr. O'Donnell brought me those documents or some other items, going through them, they didn't appear to be relevant at all to the indictment or to the indictment time frame. So I had them returned to the Detention Unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. First, only one question,

utterances.speaker: MR. INAYAT
utterances.text: Could you please explain what is -- is there any special meaning when your ERN number starts with a P or with an L?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, whenever an ERN number starts with a P, it would always mean that the material has been seized from Prijedor. So the first Prijedor and the second Prijedor collections that were seized in 1997 and in October 2000, the evidence submitted to the evidence unit was stamped with the alphabet starting with P. And L, Your Honours, starts for I believe translations, I think -- I'm not sure. If you give me a specific example of an ERN starting with an L --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: For example, list 4, 65 ter number 444, we have the English version starting sometimes with L and sometimes without L.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, this particular example you're giving would definitely mean this is a translation because the original document B/C/S is starting with a P.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, but opposed to this, 65 ter document 281, there's a translation, starts without an L.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Any specific reasons for this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can find that out for you, but I'm afraid I can't comment on this. I don't know the reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: May I ask a leading question to see if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if the L stands for "draft translation"?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification. But now the floor is for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Ostojic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Inayat. If I can direct your attention to list number 1, which is S53, I just have a couple follow-up questions on the Court's question and on the OTP's question. And -- do you have that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't have list number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Would the Court permit Madam Registrar to tender S53, which is list number 1, to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have that in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what I like, sir, with respect to testimony and issues that are before any Court, it is if you didn't understand my question, I would appreciate if you tell me. I'll try to rephrase it. To the extent that you don't know the answer, sir, I'd like you to be honest and candid with us and not speculate. Do not guess. Do not give us answers that you are unsure of. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fair enough. Look, sir, at 65 ter -- we'll look at exhibit that is marked on list number 1 as SK41A and B. You just told this Court after being questioned by the OTP that the L may stand for either translation or draft translation or a variety of those explanations. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that specific exhibit, the B/C/S ERN number specifically has in the first letter the letter L, right?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you telling us that if I were to make an analysis that this is a draft translation of a B/C/S document?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: This is clearly a mistake. The document that is in the English ERN 00403880, in fact, that is the B/C/S document. And this is clearly a mistake. And I can see another one which is entry number 2, SK18A. The English ERN is SA011169, I think again, this looks like a typo, an error.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I went through it. And with all due respect, sir, I found more than just those two examples, but we will be happy to go through them in detail with you here today. But let me ask you this, just so I'm clear: Does the L before a number mean that it's a draft of a translation, that it's a final translation, or you just don't know? And if you would like some time to examine that issue and then get back to us on that point.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I can come back to you on that point, but it does appear that L -- any ERN starting with an L is a draft translation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, Mr. Inayat, do you know -- or let me strike that. Let me ask this question this way: Do you know how to read and write the Serbo-Croatian language, B/C/S as it's commonly referred to here?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, help me with this: In your answer on page 17 of today's transcript, specifically line 4 I think it was, counsel asked you when you had duplicative documents, documents that seemed to be the same, you would make a determination and you would look at them and then you would say, yes, we found a documents in Prijedor Police Station and possibly a document in the Municipal Assembly. When would you actually come up with this analysis that those documents were the same? You didn't do it at the site, correct, during the search and seizure of December 1997?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Objection, that slightly misstates things, because he indicated they would have separate ERN numbers. Counsel is just asking them why they were grouped together on the sourcing.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If we look at the example that Mr. Inayat was somewhat unclear on where counsel pointed out I believe on list 4 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think it was list 5, 65 ter 43.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's correct. Thank you, Your Honour. 65 ter number 43, which is a third line item, let's talk about this for a second.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the analysis done, sir, to show and determine that these documents actually are the same or similar?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: First of all, I don't understand -- I can't read the B/C/S language. But for me, sometimes if I see the document which has a duplicate copy, looking at the document number and the date, it makes it obvious, if they are the same, that they are a similar copy. But in any case, the analysis would have been done when the documents are logged. So going through the log sheets, it's easy to capture such details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me understand this a little further: Is it then logical to conclude that where documents do not have two ERN numbers and wherein you provide the sourcing information, you do not list two specific sources, we can conclude reasonably that in fact that document only appeared in one place at one time. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I'm sorry, can you just repeat this once again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sure. Can we conclude from your testimony here specifically as you've explained 65 ter number 43 the converse, namely that where the sources are indicated from a document singularly, meaning one source, can we conclude that all those documents were never found in any other place?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: No, I'm afraid that cannot be concluded. I may have found two sources for one document, but that still would not mean that the same document may not have come from the third source. We may have a copy of the same document coming from the third source, but I in my searches may not have captured that particular aspect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go back to list number 1, if I may. First, some preliminary questions if you don't mind. With respect to providing us the sourcing information, it's done in order to establish for us reliability, integrity, and credibility of the source from which we, meaning all of us, have obtained those documents. Would you agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Let me give my personal opinion on this. When I do the sourcing, my emphasis is on: When was the document received, the location from where it was received or seized, the person who gave it to us, and the person who received it. So that is what my primary concern is when I'm doing the sourcing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that it's important for you to list at the very least all those three things, namely, the specific location, the person from whom you received it, and I think you said the date. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Why?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Why what?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why is it important?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Objection. Relevance, argumentative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sustained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Inayat, look at list number 1, the very first document that you have there, and let's see if you what you state as a reasonable basis for providing sources to determine if documents are reliable, credible, or have any integrity -- I'm not done; just waiting for the translators to catch up. Thank you, sir. Sorry about that. If you look at that first item on list number 1, in that very first item you don't list where the document came from. You give us this generality saying it's from Prijedor somewhere. You don't tell us from whom the document was obtained from. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't see that?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I see that. You are right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you explain to me, sir, since it may be something that you consider in providing sourcing information to this Court and to us, why do you omit that information?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Interestingly, you have picked up an example which is on the first page and it's the first entry. The book of minutes of the Prijedor SDS municipal board was a document consisting of many, many pages. I think we can even count them, maybe a hundred-plus pages. When I was doing my sourcing, I have spoken to several colleagues. They and I am definite that this particular document was seized by my colleague Eric Hanson from the SDS offices. Eric Hanson is not with the Tribunal any more. But since I couldn't find anything in black and white which would have given me the guarantee that I can write that particular source, I didn't do it. This particular book, there are several other pages from this book which have been used in Court. They may also come up in the sourcings where I have only used the word "OTP staff member seized it in Prijedor during search and seizure mission conducted on 12/12/97." But I assure you that there won't be too many examples like this. So on the one hand, I can guarantee this to the Court, that this is a document that was seized from Prijedor during the search and seizure in 1997. Personally, Your Honours, I am also certain this document, the book of minutes, came from the SDS building. But since I have not looked at any evidence which is in black and white saying that, I have refrained from mentioning the location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to clarify, I think, if I may, Mr. Inayat, you're really saying that this was seized during the December 12th, 1997, one-day seizure while you went to those four locations in Prijedor. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was during the time in which you, sir, were actually not part of the team that was seizing documents from the SDS building but were actually in the Municipal Assembly building seizing documents. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So without Mr. Eric Hanson or without this IIF form that you have, we cannot be reasonably certain with respect to this first exhibit on list number 1 that indeed it was seized from the SDS building pursuant to a legal and authorised search and seizure of December 12th, 1997. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: What I can guarantee is that this has come from the December 1997 seizure. And as I was informing the Court, that I am also certain it has come from the SDS building. But you're right. As far as this book of minutes is concerned, perhaps it may be a question to be put to Mr. Eric Hanson.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just cover a couple issues before we take the prescheduled break generally speaking, if I may. You shared with us briefly that the letter P is placed before the B/C/S numbers indicating that documents were seized from Prijedor pursuant to the December 12th, 1997, search. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If you just keep looking on list number 1, and go to the second page of list number 1, and I'd like to analyse 65 ter number 142, 65 ter number 96, and 65 ter number 89, if I may. Those three, so it's the first, second, and fourth items that appear on page 2 of list Number 1 on Exhibit S53.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I see those.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just trying to understand the methodology which you and your department used, sir. If you note on some, namely, the first two, documents seized from the SDS offices and those documents seized from the Municipal Assembly on December 12th, 1997, do not have the letter P in front of their B/C/S ERN number. But under the fourth category, documents seized from the SDS purportedly on December 12th, 1997, do have the letter P in front of the B/C/S ERN number. Can you explain to me when you used this letter P and when you don't, or is this another typo?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: The Prijedor collection from December 1997, the logging of this particular collection started some time in June of 1999. And after the logging was completed in about six, seven months' time, the material was handed and stamped with a letter starting with P. However, after we brought the collection to The Hague after the December 1997 seizure, we were -- or my team was getting ready for the trial of Dr. Milan Kovacevic. So what we did starting in early 1998 was we started reviewing the material that was seized from Prijedor, from the four locations. And during the review, we identified approximately several hundred documents that we believed were required for the Prosecution's case against Milan Kovacevic. After the material was identified, these several hundred pages that I've just spoken of, these were handed over to the evidence unit as part of evidence. And at that point, all documents that were given to the evidence unit, they were stamped with the digits 0063 starting in the beginning. So I believe that's the difference. So whenever you have documents being presented here in the Stakic case starting with the 0063, I can safely say that these are documents coming from a collection that was used for the Kovacevic prosecution.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Just a couple more question generally on this. You told on May 24th of this year when you initially testified in this case that there were two seizures that were made in Prijedor, and that you essentially seized what you deemed to be relevant documents, one on December 12th, 1997, and the other in October 2000. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes, I did say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we discussed I think three months ago the 1997 one was pursuant to a court-authorised legal and proper subpoena, and the one in October of 2000 was actually from Rule 38, the Prosecutor's directive I think as you called it. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, today you mentioned Banja Luka a little bit, and the reference to Banja Luka is really that in 1998, there was yet another Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. legal and proper search and seizure subpoena and warrant authorised by the Court of this Tribunal which permitted you and your investigators to seize documents from Banja Luka. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't mention in May of 2002 when you testified, specifically May 24th, 2002. You mentioned it today. Do you know how many documents from the Banja Luka search and seizure actually appear on lists 1 through 6 that you've prepared in connection with the case against Dr. Stakic?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I'm certain there are quite a few documents that have come from the Banja Luka collection. And if you're asking me for the exact number, then I believe I just have to run through these six exhibit lists.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you for an exact number because I think -- although I have the exact number. Would you believe me, sir, if I told you that looking at exhibits 1 through 6 that there's one document that you source that came from the search and seizure in 1998 from Banja Luka? Would you find that incredible to believe?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: You're saying that in all the documents that I have sourced, there's only one document that has come from Banja Luka search and seizure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to what you list as the source, sir.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I may have to go back and review the sourcing document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just point it out to you before we break here. If you look on the very last page of list number 6, it's the second to the last entry which is I think 65 ter number 436, provisionally given I think S228, that document, the one I'm referencing. That's the one I found. Maybe I didn't do as thoroughly as you would, sir. But can you tell me or if you come back -- can you tell me this: Do you think that the documents in Banja Luka since you amended the fourth amended complaint against Dr. Stakic and you are familiar with the three searches and seizures that were done in 1997, 1998, and 2000, do you think based upon your review of the fourth amended indictment and your understanding with discussions with the OTP in connection with issues relating to joint criminal enterprise or common plan, do you think, sir, that the documents from Banja Luka are relevant to this case?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sustained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You provided us, sir, with a list, and I appreciate that very much, last Friday of the complete set of documents that are in your possession from the search and seizure conducted in 1997 in the Prijedor Police Station, Municipal Assembly, SDS building, and Kozarski Vjesnik. That actually, from my review, was approximately 2.000 pages. That was the index. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I think that's close to the figure I had in mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, from my brief review of those documents, it seemed that a lot of the documents were from the years subsequent to 1992, namely, 1995, 1997, et cetera. Why did you seize those documents, sir, if your mandate and your thought process was to obtain and seize only "relevant documents"?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Our intention was certainly that we will only seize material that is relevant to the ICTY's mandate, which is 1991 until 1995. And I think I did explain this last time, that we had limited time at the locations with limited staff. It wasn't possible to sift through the material and to make a selection on site. So it is possible that material that was outside the ICTY's time frame may have come, as it proved later, that it did come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to those three sources we talked about where documents came from the OTP in connection with criminal proceedings before the Tribunal, specifically what I'm referencing is the 1997 search and seizure, the 1998 search and seizure, February of 1998, and the October 2000, 38 directive as you've called it from the OTP. Did the OTP, sir, also obtain documents from other sources?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your list, we can glean some -- with some certainty documents were provided to actually the trial lawyers in this case from witnesses when they arrived during their testimony. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Documents, sir, were also obtained from the OTP and your department or unit from a third source, namely called AID. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: We did receive documents from the local authorities; that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that those documents from what you call the local authorities came specifically from the division known as AID, the agency for identification and documentation?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Most documents, yes, did come from AID.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it fair to say if I use the term that the documents you received from AID in 1995, 1996, and whatever period of time it was prior to your search and seizures, that those documents were numerous?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: We received a large collection of documents from Bihac in 1996 that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does that mean? Can you quantify it for me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I object. Unless we're dealing with items that are in evidence in this case, it is going into the investigation possibly of other cases and it's just not relevant to the matter of Dr. Stakic how many documents that we're not using in this case we might have received.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Before the Court rules, I'd like to reply if I may. I think it's relevant, Your Honour, for two reasons. The Defence is contesting that the documents obviously with AID, we'll hopefully hear from the witness, are of questionable source, but the matter becomes whether or not a decision was made by the investigative team leader not to produce certain documents because he also believed that they may be unreliable. We don't know that until we lay the proper foundational question which I did; namely, the extent of the documents that were received and why if documents were received from AID as we see from each of the lists 1 through 6 that are provided, and we're going to go through those documents hopefully after the break, why other documents were not admitted. If Mr. Inayat clearly says that he made an opinion after indexing those documents that they are not relevant, we'll move forward. If he made a different conclusion in connection with those documents, I believe it's relevant and we have a right to inquire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Inayat has testified that in preparing these lists, he was given the exhibit numbers that were used in Court. He has never testified that it's his job, his responsibility, or that he selected documents for use in Court. Obviously, that's a matter for the trial lawyers. And even my opinion of the reliability of the documents is not what's at issue; it's the Court's opinion. So it doesn't make sense to ask Mr. Inayat why documents were not used or what his opinion is about documents not used in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Objection is sustained. And especially the point where we departed was the question: "Can you quantify it for me"? We should discuss with the relevant and responsible persons the question of the quality and not the question of the quantity of document received from Bihac over all. But let's have a break now until 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. And please continue immediately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Inayat, just to take up again the area that we were discussing prior to the brief break that we had. In connection with this AID agency, is it fair to say that there were two types of documents that were in essence received from them? And let me explain what I mean by "types." One, there were documents that the people who worked with AID gave to the OTP on their own initiative. And the second group of documents, if I could categorise them, are documents that the OTP in 1995 and 1996 would have requested from the AID individuals. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: The documents that were given to us in 1995, 1996, they were first reviewed by members of the Office of the Prosecutor, and a selection was made of what is required. And whatever was selected, then copies of those documents were given to us. As to your other question, the second type, occasionally we have written to the local authorities asking for specific documents. And once they have been put together by the authorities there, they either send it to us by -- through the liaison officer, who is currently in The Hague, or when our investigators visit the field, and if that material is ready for collection, it's given at that point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the information that you provide to us on lists 1 through 6 respectfully, do you indicate whether the documents specifically from the AID agency, whether those were documents that were given to the OTP on the initiative of the AID agency, or were they documents which were procured by the OTP after a specific request to AID for those documents?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: To answer this question, I would really have to look at all the requests that have been made over the years to find out what particular material has come to us after a specific request was put in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And I appreciate that. And I don't want to quarrel with that point. But my question was more limited than that. In fact, within the lists 1 through 6, when we deal with the documents specifically from the AID agency, we don't know by looking at the sourcing information that you provided us on those lists whether it came from either the initiative on its own from AID or from directives from the OTP to AID. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: That is correct. In the source column, I have not indicated that information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's look on list 1 just as an example so I can fully understand your lists and your testimony here today. On the first page of list number 1, the fifth item which is I think 65 ter number 39, are you with me?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's an item that appears on the sourcing information as something received from an OTP staff member, Kate Pearce. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, sir, whether or not Kate Pearce is a member of your criminal investigations team or unit as you've identified it here today?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Ms. Kate Pierce used to work in Team 1. She left this organisation a couple of years ago, and she was our criminal analyst.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With respect to that document since we know the search and seizures were conducted in 1997 in Prijedor, and specifically in February 1998 in Banja Luka, and then again in October of 2000 in Prijedor, can you tell us the document -- because it has a date of May 22nd, 1996, is it reasonable for me to assume that that was a document that was obtained from the AID agency?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: This particular document was brought to the Tribunal. Nobody received it in the field. This was brought to the Tribunal by the liaison officer, and Kate Pearce received it on behalf of Team 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Point out to me, sir, if you would, where does it say that the liaison officer was the one who gave that to Kate Pearce as opposed to one of the individuals who worked for and were specifically employed by the AID agency at that time?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Normally the liaison officer, when he or she comes to the Tribunal, there is a person in the office of the Prosecutor who liaises with that person, receives all documentary material that has been requested. And the contact person or the liaison officer of the OTP then distributes the documents to the teams as per relevance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I appreciate that. Just so I can understand, then, forgive me if I'm not catching this quick enough, my question to you, sir, is with respect to this document that we're discussing now, which is 65 ter number 39, SK39A and B. With that document, when you go back and do the sourcing, can you find out first whether it's possible or probable to determine exactly when Kate Pearce received the document and specifically from whom?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can I just ask the question be clarified. I think what counsel is asking about is that copy of the document. Because if I am not incorrect, there are multiple, I think five or seven, copies of that document that have been received by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may interject, Your Honour, I never object to a proposed objection from an adversary if there's a reasonable basis. However, I do take strong exception to the OTP telling us that there were many sources from the document. This witness has already testified that if there were multiple sources of a document, he would list to the best of his knowledge and belief where those documents came from and the sources of those documents. I don't mind the objection; I do mind that the OTP is testifying that there's more than one source for the document. This, as the Court knows, has been a document that the Defence has from the outset aggressively debated, objected to, and now it's an opportunity that this criminal investigator, Mr. Inayat, will share with us what the source of that information was, and in my opinion to determine whether there's any reliability to these types of documents so that the Court when making their deliberations on these exhibits ultimately will be able to fairly and accurately weigh those specific documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I think it's important to be precise, as I -- as Mr. Inayat has testified regarding multiple sourcing, when we have on this list, the lists 1 through 6, separate ERN numbers, where separate copies of the same document are in evidence in this case, he has provided the sources. On this particular document, all I ask is that it be clear that we are talking about this copy. If I recall, I could be incorrect because my memory now is going back to I think Mr. Donia, the first witness. At that time I think the Defence did raise the issue that they were going to object to this document. And I believe the Court indicated at that time that given there was a ruling pending on I believe the Bosanski Samac case, the Court asked that we wait for that ruling before litigating regarding this. There has been extensive testimony in that case regarding the various copies of this document that were received. But it's not correct to indicate that every -- that Mr. Inayat has indicated on these charts. He hasn't testified. He has indicated every copy of the document that's in the possession of the OTP -- just the ERN numbers, the particular copy that's in evidence in this case, he has indicated for each copy of those ERN numbers the source.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please, don't let us complicate the issue too much. I don't believe that your question, Mr. Ostojic, was really helpful because you asked to determine exactly when Ms. Pearce received the document. This is already answered on the document. It was the 22nd of May, 1996. I understand that your additional question is by whom she received this document, and if possible, who gave this document to the liaison officer. And I think it's a fair question, and it should be answered by the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document was received by Kate Pearce, as I've said in my source, on 22nd of May, 1996. However, if I go back to the IIF on the information index form, it should also give the information who gave it to her. Normally with these kind of documents, which are received in the Tribunal, I was talking of a procedure that the liaison officer who attends the Tribunal once a week or sometimes once in a fortnight brings with him a collection of documents that have been requested by the investigating teams. The OTP staff member who liaises with the liaison officer then receives the material and forwards that to the relevant teams. And I believe that with this particular document also, Kate Pearce received it from whoever was the OTP liaison officer with the Bosnian authorities. But I can do further searches if Your Honour instructs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let's proceed with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just stay with this document, if I may, 65 ter number 39. If a document like this, sir, is produced prior to the search and seizure and there's no reference number on the source that it ever was obtained from either the legal and proper search and seizure that was issued, the warrant issued on December 12th, 1997, can we infer from that, sir, that no such document was found in the Prijedor four locations?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think this question can't be answered because the Defence counsel himself assisted us in telling that the search and seizures were conducted 1997 onwards. So no doubt, it can't be part of this Prijedor search. So indeed, let's really be concrete. The relevant information, if necessary, would be to know who gave it to the liaison officer, the name of the liaison officer for the purposes of this case is irrelevant, I believe. It's only the question: Where does this document stem from? And I think for limited purposes, and for limited crucial documents, it can be necessary that we indeed ask for this special IIF form.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, if I may proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On in IIF form, I-F-F form, can you tell me whether or not not only do you identify the source who provided the documents to you, such as 65 ter number 39, but do you also state in that IIF form where that individual who is bringing the documents to the OTP, where he or she may have obtained such a document?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: If the IIF form is with respect to seized material, then you will find that information there. But if it is material that is being given to us by witnesses or by liaison officers from the RS or from Croatia or Bosnia, then the IIF information will only say or give the information that on such and such date the liaison officer or a witness submitted this document without going into further details as to how they received it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at any time, sir, does anyone from your unit, Team Number 1 investigations, do you ever determine what the chain of custody of that document was that you received from the individual such as Exhibit 65 ter number 39?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: This 39 document, please correct me if I am wrong, I think this is a document which discusses the variant A and B. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document does reference variant A and B, sir. It does.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I can assure you that this particular document, although we received it on 25th of May or 22nd of May, 1996, but this particular document has been verified by an OTP investigator by going into the field, and he has submitted a certified copy also. But to your question in general, a lot of documents that have come to us from the local authorities, and if they have been identified as critical, the OTP has gone back, the OTP has taken statements from local authorities or from their staff who had seized the material. The OTP has visited those locations from where the material was seized. So I believe sufficient inquiry was conducted into how the local authorities received this material.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you, sir, as the leader of Team Number 1 would be the best individual to provide us with the information in connection with those documents that we may question, correct, such as this Exhibit 65 ter number 39?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I've already told you that there's an investigator who has conducted detailed investigation into the source of this document, and he has a certified copy which is in the system.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me, just so I'm clear, on Exhibit 65 ter number 39, is there or is there not this information index form, which you identify as being an IIF, related to this document?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: There is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there would be, and within that document, you would list who the individual is who provided the document to the OTP, but you would not necessarily identify how that individual procured that document. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I believe that is the correct situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Within the IIF form -- let me ask you this, really for my own edification. The IIF has an acronym, I thought you said, of IIF, correct, or is it IIF because it stands for information index form. But the transcript from some time seems to be a little inconsistent, if I may say so, respectfully. So which is it: IIF or IFF?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: It should always be IIF, information index form.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With respect to this document 65 ter number 39, sir, do you know whether the purported certified copy that's in existence, where that document was found? Do you know if it was found in Prijedor in another municipality, and where specifically within the municipality, if you can identify for me whether it was the Municipal Assembly building, the SDS offices, the Prijedor Police Station, or Kozarski Vjesnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object on the basis that if the Court wants this information obviously the best source of this would be the investigator who conducted the examination. I think actually there was extensive testimony as I mentioned in the Samac case, and we could provide the transcript of that testimony to the Court regarding the various sources of the variant A and B document that have been received by the OTP. That would seem to make more sense than having Mr. Inayat testify about what someone told him.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We will accept any assistance --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We agree and ask Mr. Inayat to provide us with the IIF on this document in addition.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think this form IIF is an internal OTP document. And I'm not sure if that can be provided for the Defence. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just for the record, if I may Your Honour, if we just examine Exhibit S232, which is exactly a copy of that type of form which was introduced by agreement of the parties in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Can we agree that we discuss this issue after the break if you regard it as possible, please provide us with this IIF in relation to this special document. And if not, in any event, tell us the content of this document. I think we can then proceed, leaving this special document.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Generally speaking, Mr. Inayat, if you have a document that is unsigned, undated, would you think that it has more or less credibility or reliability?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This question has to be answered by the Bench.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour. But I think, as a criminal investigator, that I'm seeking merely Mr. Inayat's opinion in connection with those documents, and I'm not imputing what his testimony is; although I wouldn't like to speculate what his thoughts are as to the reliability of documents that are unsigned or undated. But with all due respect, I think it goes to the credibility of the witness depending on how the answers may or may not be forwarded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The question is not admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Inayat, we discussed earlier today the reliability, credibility, and integrity of certain documents. And we know also from your testimony on May 24th, 2002, as well as your testimony here today that the first search and seizure that was done for Prijedor documents were, in fact, on December 12th, 1997.
