With that backdrop, sir, would it be fair to state that the indictments that were rendered and provided against the accused, namely, Dr. Milomir Stakic, Simo Drljaca, and Dr. Milan Kovacevic, the basis for these documents were exclusively the documents that were provided to and given to the OTP by the AID agency?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Objection. Relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sustained. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Specifically Mr. Inayat, you referenced that you reviewed the indictment in connection with Dr. Stakic. On paragraph number 5 of that indictment is references specifically 65 ter number 39. Is it fair to state, sir, that the reference to that document is specifically and exclusively the items that were produced to the OTP by the AID agency employees?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The witness can't be held responsible for the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Shall I move on, Your Honour? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if I'm going to assess a document, help me with this: Do you think that it's reasonable and important for me to know the individual who may be giving me that document as to the type of person he is, whether he has a criminal record, and whether or not he has been charged with fraud, specifically fraud perpetrated on changing and misrepresenting official documents? Do you think that might be something that would interest me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, I didn't hear it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Rhetorical question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let me try it this way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Inayat, you're familiar with the individuals at AID who actually have now recently in the year 2000 been charged with, among other things, criminal activity including terrorist acts as well as fraud in preparation of official and formal documents on behalf of their government, are you not?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I've heard about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, did you ever go back to say: "Are those the same individuals who provided me documentation as a member of the OTP in connection with any indictments that I may have participated in or any search and seizures that I may have participated in to determine whether or not those documents are actually credible, reliable, and would have any integrity to withstand a court of law?"

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: As far as search and seizures are concerned, the OTP was not assisted in any way by the agency that you're referring as AID. As for the other documents that were given to us in 1995, 1996, and in the following years, my personal opinion is that none of the persons were involved or have been charged with the crimes that you are alleging. So I don't have any reason to go back and verify the credibility of those documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Forgive me, sir. I'm not alleging anything against these individuals. Quite frankly, is it fair to state that there were five specific individuals who were charged by their very own government who were at one time employed by the AID agency which was providing documents to you, that they are the ones, that government -- against those five individuals who provided the OTP documents, they are the ones making the allegations of fraud among other illegal criminal conduct against these individuals? Did you ever go back, sir, to determine whether or not any of those five individuals were part or within a group of individuals that were supplying to the OTP documentation which was, in my opinion, unsigned, undated, unverified in 1995 and 1996 which was actually the basis of the indictments against, among others, Dr. Milomir Stakic?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Like I said this earlier this morning, that in 1995, 1996, members of the Office of the Prosecutor went and made a selection from amongst of hundreds of thousands of pages that were made available to us for inquiry. And after making a selection, a couple of years later, investigators from the Office of the Prosecutor in 1999, in the year 1999, they went back and made certified copies. And I don't believe even today that any of those documents were forged. No information has come to us specifically in the team area that these documents could have been forged.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't believe the witness answered the question. I think he had answered it previously, but the question again was whether the five -- counsel says five individuals who were charged with some crimes, fraud, provided documents that were used in this case, to Mr. Inayat's knowledge.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm afraid it's not in my knowledge that any of these five persons had provided any documents to Team 1 directly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The trial counsel for the OTP earlier mentioned to the court in your presence, sir, the issues that may have arisen in connection with the AID documents Sanski Most. Is your team at all responsible for that municipality?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: My team and there are a couple of other teams that were responsible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Being the leader of your unit 1 or Team 1, the criminal investigator, did you know that in Sanski Most, there was an agreement, and again I'm saying this parenthetically if I may, and a stipulation if you will that in fact the documents provided in Sanski Most from the AID people were, in fact, fraudulent?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Counsel is testifying. How can he ask him if he knows something that's not established in this case. He can ask him if he believes that to be true. I frankly don't know what counsel is referring to, and I suspect it's taken out of context from the Brdjanin/Talic case, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with that at all, sir?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar, sir, that in the Omarska trial that was conducted several months ago that a witness who testified in connection with signatures that were provided in either documents or witness statements with the assistance purportedly of AID employees were actually falsified, that the signatures of the witnesses from whom the AID are procuring information to be used at an international criminal Tribunal were falsified? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Objection. Your Honour, we can litigate the issue of what went on in another case here and go into great detail. But we're talking apparently about a witness who did not testify in this case. I think it's -- the probative value is outweighed by the amount of time it will take to litigate a very peripheral issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think as a starting point, a possible starting point, the witness may answer the question whether or not he's aware of that what was enclosed in the question we just heard from the OTP.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I've heard about this particular incident in the Omarska trial when this thing came up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please slow down a little bit for the benefit of the interpreters, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With respect to the documents that are provided on your lists 1 through 6 respectfully, there's approximately in my count 15 documents that were submitted by the AID agency. Correct? You don't have to count them. Just generally do you have an idea how many there were?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: There are quite a few.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me show you if I may --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May I ask the Court to mark as an exhibit an article that appeared in Slobodna Bosna on June 6th, 2000. I apologise for not having adequate copies, but I'm convinced for a number of reasons that the OTP has the article because it seems to have been previously used and identified in another matter. If we could have that marked, I would ask the witness about this article.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May we have the next D number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It would be D24, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could I see the article before it is...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, of course. You have to be heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Apparently it's not translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Are you kind enough also to provide the Bench with a copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I would be kind enough to do so, Your Honour. I will do that at the first opportunity at the break. If I can just ask him general questions in connection with that. I didn't anticipate it would be necessary at this time, but since we're on the issue I think we should exhaust this issue. If the Court would like, I could come back to the matter after our lunch break --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm not prepared to discuss an issue when we don't have the document before us.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough, Your Honour. Would the usher be kind enough to remove the Slobodna Bosna article dated the 6th of June, 2002, from the witness at this time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, with respect to these IIF form, I-I-F form, that you had, we've heard from other witnesses respectfully and also from you that documents that were seized specifically pursuant to a legal and authorised search and seizure warrant such as those seized on December 12th, 1997, that you would "immediately" fill out the IIF form. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: You mean at the time of the seizure?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: No, we wouldn't do that. This procedure has been followed once the material was brought to the Tribunal, and evidence which was considered relevant to the case, that was IIFed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And all other evidence that you deem not relevant was not IIFed. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: All material that was seized from Prijedor, I can say, wasn't IIFed. It was stamped and put into the evidence unit after it was given its unique ERN range. But evidence that was selected for the Court or the evidence that was to be turned into exhibits, once that was identified, it was IIFed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just understand you if I may. Within the IIF form itself, it has a line that asked for a chain of custody? Whether or not it was properly followed. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: There was a chain of custody field in the IIF form.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a criminal investigator, sir, what does that mean to you "chain of custody"?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: It's a mechanism of recording evidence that is turned into court and to also show who has handled it from the time it was seized until the time it comes to the Court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a mechanism, sir, exactly on those three areas that we discussed this morning to ensure that documents that are being used in a criminal proceeding are reliable, are credible, and can be seen with at least having some integrity. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sustained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With respect to the Prijedor documents, I'm confused as to your testimony. Is it that none of the documents seized from Prijedor on December 12th, 1997, were initially IIFed, I-I-F?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: The whole Prijedor collection has not been IIFed, only material that has been identified as evidence to be used in court has been IIFed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when that documentation was made to use evidence or documents in court for the trial of Dr. Milomir Stakic, who went back to determine whether or not there was a proper chain of custody that was followed?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: In the case of the Prijedor search and seizure, I think I did point this out in my testimony which only was given in May, that it was a very large collection seized by the OTP for the first time. And once the material was brought back to the Tribunal, there was some discussion about processing it and the procedures to be used. I remember there was also some discussion that we should also make copies and provide those to the authorities in Prijedor. So the collection stayed in my office, which was shared by another trial attorney, for a considerable time, and the logging started in June 1999. The person in charge of the evidence unit then decided that this material will not be considered as chain of custody because it has been not given to the evidence unit immediately and because it was with the investigation team. So the chain of custody -- this material was not to be considered as chain of custody. So it was lifted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please forgive me, I don't understand what it means, so it was lifted. Really what you're saying is that the issue with respect to chain of custody in connection with the documents that were seized in Prijedor in December of 1997 were completely ignored. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: What I'm saying is that the Prijedor collection within the OTP is not considered as chain of custody material any more. It is being considered a collection like any other documentary material.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Help me understand this, sir: If you have a proper and legal search and seizure warrant and you go to the place exactly in which the warrant permits you to go, and hypothetically let's say it's the Municipal Assembly building in Prijedor, and you go there on December 12th of 1997, don't you think that, at least from your perspective as a criminal investigator, finding that document there would give you a little more weight in terms of its reliability, credibility, and integrity than a document that a stranger or a third party who happens to have been indicted, charged with fraud, among other criminal acts, that it would have more weight?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sustained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Inayat, explain to me then when, in your opinion, as a criminal investigator chain of custody is relevant or important?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just for my edification have a basis for the objection, if I may, because objections in general are generally speaking, at least for me, deemed to be foundational objections. I don't necessarily believe that the objection was foundational because the question clearly asked for his specific experience as a criminal investigator. So if I may just be assisted on that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let me make it quite clear, if you include in one question five different issues, and then ask more or less hypothetical questions, there is no need to give any additional reason for this objection. And therefore, this objection was sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Inayat, can you tell me what the procedure is in your unit as to when documents be considered to fall within the category of chain of custody? When do you make that decision?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: If the source of the document is giving me an original document, not a photocopy, but an original document, I would definitely want it to be chain of custody. If I go on a search and seizure mission where most of the time you tend to collect original documents, I would prefer to do a chain of custody on that material. If I'm given an artifact like, say, a revolver or any firearm which I have collected -- if I have collected it from the crime scene or if somebody has given it to me, I would want that to be chain of custody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I hope I don't interrupt the line of questions by the Defence, but Mr. Inayat, don't you regard it as necessary when on the basis of such a search and seizure order you seize documents, that you have an inventory, a list of documents, where a document has been found, in which room a document has been found? And can't we trace based on these documents where the documents in fact has been?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, when we do a search and seizure, the investigators have with them a form called the evidence register form. The investigator is supposed to inventorise on that evidence register form everything that he has seized. However, in the case of Prijedor, Your Honours, we did fill out evidence register forms. But because of the limited number of time that we had, it was not possible to go through each and every page of what was being seized and to record particulars or you know the details. So for example, if I went into the Municipal Assembly building in December 1997 and I went to, say, room number 28, because I remember that from that particular room I did seize considerable documentation, I probably seized 38 folders, huge folders, with multiple copies in each folder. So the procedure that I adopted was by filling out the evidence register form, when I picked up one folder, say, which had a green hard copy, I would enter into the evidence register form that seized from this location a folder which has a green hard copy. And similarly, going to the second folder trying to explain if it has a plastic folder, and also in most cases what I did was I also gave the information from the first page, what was the title, the folder. It could have been mail, internal correspondence, it could have been any number of things. So that was the only thing possible in that limited time to do. So we have the evidence register forms where such information has been put in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So I understand correctly that even though you had only limited time, it would be possible, for example, on the basis of this additional document to find out whether or not a document was found in a room that was allegedly for a certain period of time Dr. Stakic's office.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we are talking of the municipal building only, just to give an example, we went to three different locations room 28, room 38, and the archive section. My ERF form, evidence register form, gives me information about those folders. What I need to do is after I have been given information of an ERN range which comes from the Prijedor collection, I have to go back to my evidence register form and the logs, and by using those two documents, I should be able to identify a particular document that you are interested in and to be able to say to this Court what room it has come from. I may even be able to tell you what folder it has come from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification. The Defence may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Inayat, I just want to understand. On May 24th, 2002, you stated on page 3.514, on line 7, this is during your questioning by Mr. Koumjian for the OTP, you go on to say among other things: "If the evidence has been seized, then it has to be treated differently. For example, if I am on a search and seizure mission, and I have seized materials under a search warrant issued by this Chamber or by the Tribunal, then I have to complete a chain of custody form immediately. I have to write down the exact details of immediately when that happens. And then the chain of custody form, basically then, is brought back it the evidence..." And for the record, there's other things that you mention in this answer. Just so that I understand in plain English, did you fill out the chain of custody form for the Prijedor documents as you told us in May of 2002, or did you not fill out the chain of custody form for the Prijedor documents as what I believe you told us just recently?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: The evidence register form which is the chain of custody form was filled out immediately on the day of the seizure, and I stand behind that. But like I said, and I was trying to explain this to the Court, because of the limited period of time we did not have the opportunity to give the kind of description which would have been preferable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So for each document that has been used at the trial, there has an IIF form, and for each document that was used in the trial, it would be easy for us to assume that within the IIF form, chain of custody question mark undoubtedly would be marked yes because for all of the Prijedor documents you filled out this register form as you've identified it. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Evidence register form.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Evidence registry form. Of the 40.000 documents, in excess of 100 pages of material that were seized from December 12th, 1997, did you sir at any time determine how many of those documents were used or identified on your list 1 through 6?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: The first thing I would like to do is I would like to correct myself because from the 24th May testimony, I had said 40.000 documents. And I believe that the understanding between you and me was that you won't hold me to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I won't.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: And I think it's possibly preferable if I just give you the figures. The total number of pages seized from the Prijedor collection in December 1997 was approximately 53.000, and not more than a hundred thousand, and certainly not 40.000 documents. If you don't mind, I'd just like to read your question once again. Yes. The complete source list that I have created which probably has been submitted in court, I can go through that and give you the exact number of documents from the Prijedor collection that has been identified and used. I'm sorry, if that was your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, it was, and you answered it, thank you. With respect to those 53.000 pages of document that were seized on December 12th, 1997, do you, sir, know how many different documents there were? I appreciate you telling us that the page number was overstated, if I will, to use a neutral term from 100.000 to 53.000. But you also shared with us last time on May 24th, 2002, that 40.000 documents were seized. Did you go back to determine how many documents were seized?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: 40.000 documents or pages which were over a hundred thousand I've already said was wrong; it was 53.000 pages. What I have done in the interim is that I've tried to count the pages which have come from different locations, for example, December 1997 search and seizure, police station, there were 31.000 pages approximately. Municipal Assembly building, 16.972 pages. The SDS offices, 4.504 pages approximately. From the radio station, there were nine tapes, audiotapes. And from the Kozarski Vjesnik, there were 164 papers. What I can tell you right now is that I believe something like 14.000 to 15.000 documents were seized, which probably were about 53.000 pages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of those 14 to 15.000 documents that were seized, would it surprise you, sir, that within your list 1 through 6 respectfully, only 100, exactly 100 documents, were used in this trial against Dr. Stakic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I can't see any relevance.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I will move on if I may, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it surprise you, sir, that within the documents in your list 1 through 6 that from the SDS building where the search and seizure was conducted on December of 1997, only 16 documents were used - do you know that - out of the 4.504 that you claim were seized from that institution?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, these are simply arguments that counsel can make to the Court at the appropriate time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I just be heard, Your Honour, we need to get the evidence, I believe, respectfully in before we can make an argument about. So if I may just be given a little latitude to ask the question in connection with the three other locations. And if counsel continues to object, I would stipulate that he has a standing objection and we would respect whatever ruling the Court makes in connection with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No, but please tell me: What can be the relevance whether or not a witness is apprised of a number of documents used in court all of this number of documents? It doesn't help at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Inayat --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may proceed, Your Honour. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Inayat, do you know that in fact out of the 4.504 documents that were seized from SDS on December 12th, 1997, only 16 of those documents were used in the trial against Dr. Stakic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: In fact, Your Honour, Mr. Inayat wouldn't know it; he would only know what's on the list. And secondly, the lists speak for themselves and the documents in court. If counsel represents that he has counted them, I'll accept that representation. We can stipulate to it. But it's already in evidence, the lists are there with the sources.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Agreed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Inayat, if you look -- and we'll go through the documents hopefully in short order. Did you at any time, sir, find out or learn that of approximately 6 out of the 14 documents that purports to have the signature of Dr. Milomir Stakic were found to be by a forensic expert offered by the OTP were not necessarily found to be reliable and he could not conclude with reliability that that was the signature of Dr. Stakic. And further, if you make the analysis, sir, those documents that were submitted by the OTP which purport to bear the signature of Dr. Milomir Stakic were documents that were given to the OTP by the AID agency employees?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. If we want to argue the reliability of documents, I'm prepared to do that now. But counsel is simply using the examination to make his arguments. First of all, the handwriting report does not in any way indicate that the documents are not reliable; that's a misstatement of the report. But this witness has not to my knowledge even had the report. And his reading of the report is not what's important. Your Honours are the ones who will decide based upon reading the report and hearing from the witness what reliability to give to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sustained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Earlier, on May 24th, 2002, sir, you testified in essence that questionnaires within your unit are not utilised for interviewing witnesses or respectfully victims for the issues related to a particular trial. But you do note, sir, that interviews and interview forms, namely, questionnaires, are utilised for interviewing accused. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I think what I said in my last testimony was that I do not use questionnaires for interviewing witnesses. And I'm not sure if my investigators working in my team have ever told me that they use questionnaires. And finally what I said was that I would use questionnaires when interviewing an accused, and I have used a questionnaire when interviewing one accused.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Did you make any attempts to interview Dr. Milomir Stakic?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I believe it was a day or two later of Mr. Stakic's arrest and transfer to the Detention Unit that I went to see him. And I did ask him if he was prepared to be interviewed. And Dr. Stakic stated that he would have to discuss this first with his lawyer who had still not been assigned. And finally, I requested him that if you do make a decision, after discussing this with your lawyer, to be interviewed by the OTP, please communicate that information to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you at that time, sir, when you had a conversation with Dr. Stakic, did you have the interview questionnaire for accused that may be utilised in your possession?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: The purpose of that initial contact was to find out whether Mr. Stakic would be interested in being interviewed. And had he said yes, then we would have discussed the dates for the interview at which point I would have prepared a questionnaire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you at that interview with Dr. Stakic advise him of his right to remain silent and that he has a right to retain counsel?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Mr. Stakic was advised of the rights, and I did read him those rights.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With respect and in connection with this issue of witnesses, on May 24th, 2002, on page 3562 specifically, you state that you were personally not aware of having interviewed any witnesses specifically for Dr. Stakic's case. True or false?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I may have -- or should I say I definitely have interviewed a couple of witnesses who may have testified in the Stakic trial. But I think in my earlier testimony, what I probably wanted to say was that I have not sought out witnesses to interview them specifically on Dr. Stakic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what I thought. That's why I'm asking you that. Because I went back and did a little search and found that there were actually no less than ten witnesses that you were involved with in taking statements from which were either identified under 65 ter numbers or actually witnesses who were called to testify viva voce in front of the Tribunal or pursuant to Rule 92 bis. Did you go back, sir, to determine how many witnesses you actually were involved with and interviewed that were utilised in this case?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I haven't particularly tried to verify this information. But I remember that during the preparation for the trial of Dr. Milan Kovacevic, I was interviewing witnesses who may have been identified subsequently to come and testify for Dr. Stakic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you ever, sir, during the time that you were interviewing witnesses, whether it was for the case against the late Dr. Milan Kovacevic or for Dr. Milomir Stakic here, did you ever, sir, instruct and direct a potential witness to go in the field and to have a discussion with an accused?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I'm sorry, can you please repeat this question again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time period that you were obtaining information in connection with pending or secret indictments, as well as during the time period that you were preparing for the trial of the late Dr. Milan Kovacevic, did you direct any witnesses or instruct them to go to the accused in order to obtain additional information?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I honestly don't recall ever having requested a witness that I interviewed to go and speak to Dr. Stakic. But if you have a specific example that you're aware of, if you tell me, I'll be very honest about it. But I have no recollection of doing such a thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not accusing you of doing it, sir; I'm just curious to know if you would ever do something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: That theoretical question, I think, isn't relevant to the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me go back. Let me back up, Your Honour, if I may be permitted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, specifically in connection with a witness identified before this Tribunal as Mr. Edward Sebastian Vulliamy, a witness that claims to be a fact witness, did you or anyone on your criminal investigation Team Number 1, including all the criminal investigators, including the attorneys who comprised part of that Unit Number 1, including all the interpreters that are within that group, all those seven to ten individuals that you've identified, did any of you tell Mr. Vulliamy to go back to Prijedor, interview these people, and find out what it is they can say because potentially we'll use it in an indictment that is now secret but hopefully will soon to become public?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Can you please restate the name. We didn't --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Edward Sebastian Vulliamy. Is that the name?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He's a witness. Right?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're aware of him. Right?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know or have any information with respect to Mr. Vulliamy whether anyone from your team would ever do something like that?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I met Mr. Vulliamy several months ago, and I can state this on authority, and I don't think Mr. Vulliamy would ever rebut this. I never suggested to him that he should go and talk to Mr. Stakic in Prijedor because I knew that Mr. Stakic is not living in Prijedor any more. He's somewhere in Belgrade. Mr. Vulliamy, when he came to testify in the Tadic trial way back in 1996, 1997, I wasn't with the Team 1 at that time. I was part of another investigation team. So if something has happened during that period, I'm afraid I would not be able to make any comments because I'm not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course, and that's fair, Mr. Inayat. Really, I'm not asking about the Tadic trial. I'm asking about a trial that you've already shared with us you were involved in; namely, the late Dr. Milan Kovacevic. You were involved in that trial. Mr. Vulliamy testified in that case. What about that, sir? Specifically not you, if you asked Vulliamy, but did anyone from your team tell a witness like Mr. Vulliamy: "Go out there, demand that you be seen with this witnesses, obtain information from them so that we can utilise it in what is soon to become a public indictment but at that time was a sealed indictment"?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Such a request to Mr. Vulliamy by anybody during the Kovacevic trial was not made in my presence. However, if you have the information of the person who made such a request, I think it would be best to put this question to that person because it wasn't made in my presence, and I'm not aware of any such thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're aware of the testimony that Mr. Vulliamy gave in the Kovacevic case, are you not?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Objection. Whether he's aware of it or not, it will speak for itself. And Mr. Vulliamy will also be here to speak for himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sustained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, at any time as a criminal investigator having graduated from Islamabad in Pakistan and Exeter and obtaining a degree in international investigations did you ever, sir, as a criminal investigator ask a witness to interview a potentially accused individual on behalf of your offices?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The question is not relevant for our case. And, in addition, the witness may not testify on issues related to former cases relevant on his domestic national level.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just for the record, I was merely utilising his background and extensive experience that the witness does have in connection with criminal investigations. And I would just would like to have been able to make a comparative analysis that in no country at no place in the world would a criminal investigator be permitted to utilise a witness, a fact witness and ultimately a witness that would be used in a trial against an accused, to interview him without the right to his counsel or to inform him properly of what his rights may be. And I'm just curious to know from Mr. Inayat if that exists anywhere to his knowledge with his extensive experience in the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Objection. I could state my grounds, but I don't think it's necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The grounds are self-evident, and the Defence counsel shouldn't be too optimistic on this issue, on the outcome of such research.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With respect to interviews taken perhaps of the accused in this case, I know you identified at least one that you have taken, the Court from time to time has suggested that both parties may consider calling, if I can say it respectfully, individuals that are accused. Do you know who the individual is who would have the interview questionnaire and the answers provided of the accused Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if counsel wishes to obtain information from the OTP, I and the other trial attorneys can speak on behalf of the OTP. We are not going to discuss in open Court investigations that may have been ongoing or information obtained, but we can deal with this through the counsel and the Court. But it's not proper to be asking a witness about other investigations, and to be honest, he is asking about an investigation I don't know anything about at the moment but I could find out. But whatever it is, it should not be discussed in open court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think this approach is not only fair, but it's the approach you would find in most jurisdictions.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Similarly Mr. Inayat, who would be the individual I would seek to obtain information in connection with the interview questionnaire and answers provided by one an accused by the name of Dr. Biljana Plavsic? Based upon information and belief, she has offered some testimony. Who would that individual be?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, counsel has asked the exact same question substituting a different name. I don't know what the purpose of it is, but I find it actually completely improper to do that knowing the Court has just ruled it's an improper question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Indeed, we would need some explanation on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I can share it with the Court if you would like now. Or at any time the Court is prepared or willing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think in the moment, it's not relevant as a question to the witness before us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On May 24th, 2002, sir, I asked you whether or not you as a team leader of Team 1 for the Stakic trial, whether or not you did the verification of certain documents that were submitted pursuant to Rule -- I'm just waiting for the... Rule 68. Your response in essence, sir, on page 3569 was that another individual whose name you identified Ms. Suellen Taylor was an individual you would have to check for and verify whether or not the documents provided for the Defence and Dr. Stakic pursuant to that rule were complete, exhaustive, and accurate. Based on that, have you since the three months of your prior testimony made any such inquiries?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: In May 2002, when I had said before this Court that personally I had not been involved in the Rule 68 searches, I was correct. However, since then, I think within a couple of weeks after that, we initiated another very big Rule 68 search. We identified 1.600 names of witnesses from Prijedor. The list was then distributed amongst many investigators and analysts within the team. And to share the workload, I personally also did a search on I believe about 80 witnesses. So far, we have concluded searches regarding 1.100 witnesses. I believe that in the next five to six weeks, we will have completed the Rule 68 searches on these 1.600 witnesses. And personally what I have done, I did identify a few documents which I considered to be Rule 68 which I then forwarded to the trial attorneys, the legal officers within the team. And that is exactly what other investigators are also doing. So it is expected that the search results will be forwarded to this Court and to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I appreciate it, Mr. Inayat. Just so I can be clear on it, when you say you produced it to the trial attorneys, it's not an issue that you would produce it to the Defence attorneys. You would give it obviously to the OTP trial attorneys, and they would do what is required of them in terms of tendering the documents to the Defence, among others. Correct? Or did you submit something to us that we don't know about?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Let me correct myself. During this search which has been conducted by investigators and analysts, if we come up or identify documents that we consider are Rule 68, the investigators forward these to the legal officers -- I'm sorry when I said trial attorneys on the team. The legal officers within Team 1. Those legal officers then review the material to confirm that this is Rule 68. And that particular exercise, as I said, should be completed in five to six weeks' time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Just a couple quick questions if I may in connection with matters that we can hopefully clean up before the break. If you turn to page 2 of your list number 1, that should be before you, which is exhibit, for the record, S53. I haven't asked the question yet, sir, so I'm not sure you're looking in the right spot. I just want you to have the list before you. It's my understanding that when an exhibit or a document is created or used by an expert, say a demographer hypothetically, that she would rely on certain information because it's, as we said earlier, credible, reliable, there's integrity, correct? Yes?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 2 of this list number 1, you yourself have created certain documents that were utilised by an OTP demographer, namely 65 ter number 857, which is Exhibit Number S1, I believe. Correct? Which is the Prijedor ethnic composition map.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if I, a Defence attorney such as myself --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure if there's an objection or not. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Well, I don't think this witness can talk about what was utilised by the demographer. He's talking about the demographer's actual conclusions. I think the demographer testified on her own what her sources were, and actually I don't recall her ever saying that she relied upon anything produced by Mr. Inayat other than perhaps dsy an illustration of her testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If we can just have the witness perhaps clarify. That might be the case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Inayat, I apologise. With respect to this document, S1, it states the source, created by OTP staff member, Mr. Inayat, yourself, on 22/3/02. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that something that, sir, you prepared after reading or understanding the conclusions based or made by Madam Eva Tabeau? Or is that something that you did before she was even asked to prepare her report in this case?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: This map was prepared much earlier than when she came and testified, much earlier. After preparing it, I may have IIFed it on 22nd of March, 2002, but I remember this particular map was also used in the pretrial brief of Mr. Brdjanin and General Talic. So this was prepared a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not so long, only March 22nd. Right?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: What I mean is that this particular date is when I probably IIFed it and put it in evidence. The actual map was created maybe a year ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sir, where would you get information which would assist you in creating what has become evidence in a case utilised by other witnesses such as a demographer, among others, where would you obtain information in order to be able to create an ethnic composition map? I mean, did you interview people? Did you look at the census as Dr. Tabeau did? Did you look at the voter registration forms to create what you state is an ethnic composition map? Did you do any of that?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: The thing is that UNPROFOR gave us these maps in 1996, later also in 1997, 1998, for each of the municipalities which has the ethnic composition. But when I was preparing these maps, I looked at the ones that were given to us by UNPROFOR, and also by the census -- the 1991 census. So I used information from those two sources to prepare my maps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just help me with this, before the break, so you're relying on information that was provided to you from 1996. Correct? Is that what your testimony is?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: From 1996 onwards, over the years, UNPROFOR, United Nations protection force in Bosnia, they had provided us copies of ethnic composition of all Bosnian municipalities. That was one source. And secondly, the 1991 census report. I used these two sources to prepare my maps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able within those maps that you received in 1996 onward to determine what the ethnic population movement was in the Prijedor Municipality in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: As far as the movement of ethnic groups is concerned from 1992, I used a document that we seized from the CSB building in Banja Luka in February of 1998 which clearly indicated the population of a particular municipality before 1992 and after the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if that document that you seized from the Banja Luka seizure in February 1998 whether -- I couldn't find it on your lists 1 through 6. Do you know where it appears?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: It has been definitely disclosed in several cases, but I'm not sure if it has been disclosed in the Stakic case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I only find one document from that 1998, but I just have a couple more questions and we'll get to it real quick. With respect to the document that you have relating to ethnic groups and movement, my question was specific: Did you obtain any information to determine what the movement of population was in the Prijedor Municipality for 1992? Not before 1992 and after 1992, because it just gives us too wide of a range and I can't certainly handle that amount of information. But do you know what the information was for the population of Prijedor in, let's say, January of 1992 and what it was after there was an influx of Serb refugees from Croatia? And then, comparatively speaking, do you know what the population and movement of ethnic groups were, let's pick the end of September 1992, since that's the time frame chosen for the indictment against Dr. Milomir Stakic? Have you ever done that analysis?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: The ethnic composition map that I have prepared, I have used information from the 1991 census to show the population at the beginning of 1992. And I have used the CSB document which we seized in February 1998 to show what the population was in Prijedor in 1995. Personally, I have not reviewed any material to show the movement of population in 1992, but I believe that the demographers did that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They might still be doing it, but I don't want to quarrel with you on that, sir. With respect to the movement of population and specifically the count against Dr. Milomir Stakic relating to deportation, do you know if the 1991 census that you relied upon to determine the number of people by their ethnic composition in the Prijedor Municipality in 1991 did not include the number of refugees that were coming from Croatia within that census?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I don't recall having gone into that much detail when looking at the 1991 census. All I remember is, and as you can also see from my ethnic composition maps for all the municipalities that I did, that I was looking at the three main groups, the population of the Serbs, the population of the Croats, and the population of the Muslims. And I was not looking at figures for Yugoslavs or those who call themselves others and refugees. So I was only interested in these three main groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure if it's an appropriate time but...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The trial stays adjourned until 2.30. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.58 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. And continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours, Mr. Inayat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In connection with with your testimony here today, we were able - and we appreciate the Court giving us time - to provide you with a copy of an exhibit, or if the usher would be kind enough to present that to you, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. of Slobodna Bosna dated in June of 2002. We have copies for the Court and the OTP as well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can I just inquire, is that translated or is the witness going to be shown an article in a language he does not understand?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: For the purposes of my cross-examination I would like initially to ask the witness whether he has seen the article as it appeared in the B/C/S language, and the article itself, as I think the OTP knows, has been translated and we are also providing the translated version of the article as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This seems to be a very tricky exercise we haven't had yet until now. Why is this necessary, I as a witness personally would object immediately if I ever saw a document in a language you don't understand. But apparently we have now an English translation, but this seems to be a Supreme Court --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may clarify without testifying, just for purposes of clarification, there are actually three documents that the Court should receive as well as the witness, one being the B/C/S version of the article as it appeared in Slobodna Bosna in June of 2002. Then also the translation or translated versions of both the article that appears within that B/C/S document as well as the text which is reprinted in the article which relates to the decision of the Supreme Court that the Court mentioned. So you should have all three, two English translations, and one in B/C/S, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Not yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I don't have --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Forthcoming. Forthcoming.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So this article on Nato Opotakora [phoen], this would be D24?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's what the Court mentioned I think earlier --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May it please be confirmed by the registry, D24A and B.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. I don't see any relevance of this document to the proceedings in this case. As I see it, these are -- to be honest, I haven't had a chance to read it in full, but just from what I've glanced in the few seconds I've had the document, the article appears to be talking about a letter regarding a 1996 IFOR operations and the possibility that there was terrorists in Bosnia, that that was directed against. There are some names here, none of the names as far as I know are connected in any way, as far as I know, to the Stakic case or to the exhibits that are the subject of apparently the cross-examination. We could have the indictment against Osama Bin Laden in the Court, but I don't think that's relevant either to the charges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think both parties today should try not to overstate. I understood from the line of questions that the question on the IDP, the reliability of IDP, and the work of IDP. Correct? Is this in the line of question?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the -- maybe I'm lost -- I'm at a loss at the moment, but I'm unfamiliar at the moment with the actual acronym. Is the AID organisation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: AID, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I had it incorrect in the translation. Thank you. I can state the argument reasonably briefly, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately we don't have at the moment from Mr. Inayat the actual source from which the documents have been presented to the OTP. Based upon information and belief, we believe that the individuals who actually were in charge and specifically produced those documents to the OTP relating to Dr. Stakic's case were the individuals that are identified on the exhibits that we've tendered to the Court. Specifically we're not interested in the allegations with respect to terrorist activities that these persons may have been charged with. We are specifically interested in the forgery, forgery of both documentation and forgery of foreign passports and travel Visas from this group of individuals. Although I appreciate my learned friend's comments that these individuals are not connected with this case, I think it's a leap of faith to say that because Mr. Inayat also has not provided us with that source to make that reasonable conclusion. They were and are employed, as reflected in that document, in senior and leading positions within AID, were responsible at the time reference, namely 1995 and 1996, to procure, obtain, and to gather data on behalf of and for the OTP. We believe that the information will be that these five individuals from time to time were involved directly or indirectly with the documents that are at issue. Specifically, we're concerned with this document that we discussed this morning, but also in particular six documents that were allegedly signed by Dr. Stakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if counsel could tell us what the basis is for his belief that these individuals were involved in the documents at issue, I could see -- we would be coming much closer to relevance. I'm not aware of it, but perhaps counsel has some information I'm not aware of, that these individuals are involved with the documents that are at issue in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Indeed, quite frankly said, it would be -- should be from the point of view of the Defence more than only wishful thinking.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I wish it was only wishful thinking, quite frankly. But if we look at how the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina through their indictment and criticism of these five individuals identified them in the capacity in which they were employed with AID, I think it's not only a reasonable assumption, but I think it's rather logical that these individuals were in some way connected with the documents both in Bihac and Sanski Most, in Kljuc, and in other municipalities from which Mr. Inayat has received documents or people from his staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think it's the question of the OTP is only fair, to ask whether you have any kind of link between these names and the documents in our case, or if it's only the idea that this could be.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's more than speculation, Your Honour, but the onus I think should be on Mr. Inayat to give us the source specifically so that we can be clear as to whether or not any of these individuals actually participated in any fashion in producing these documents. If he comes back in his analysis and tells us that these individuals have never met any members of our staff Team 1, have not produced any of the documentation which we're referencing in our lists 1 through 6 and that we, meaning the OTP at this time, did not as previously testified by Mr. Inayat, did not request from these five heads of the AID division any information. If the Court would recall, information and documents were received from AID in two forms, one voluntarily submitted by them to the OTP and then subsequently at the specific written request by the OTP. To whom would the OTP write other than to heads of these various units and departments whose names we believe are revealed in those letters and correspondence which we don't have as well as those that are indicated in this newspaper article and indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The article stems from the 6th of June, 2002. Do you have any idea whether or not these persons worked with the idea already at that time when representatives of the OTP received documents from AID?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Based upon information and belief, Your Honour, the first sentence on the second page of the exhibit that's translated clearly revealed that the period in question where there's issue relating to illegal criminal activity including forgery occurred during 1995 up to February 15th, 1996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Until now, we have followed as regards the tendered OTP documents very liberal policy, and the same has to be true when it comes to documents tendered by the Defence. Therefore, always recalling that the admission into evidence does not yet mean that the Bench comes to the conclusion that there is any or to what extent there is probative value, these documents are admitted into evidence as D24A and B. And I have no doubt that the Defence will immediately afterwards ask the witness, and there comes then the relevance of these documents, whether or not -- or the representatives of the OTP, especially the witness before us, ever had contact with concrete persons in the ADP [sic], especially those mentioned here, or only with the organisation as such. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. May I proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just for the record, I'm confused about which exhibits have which numbers because what I have is two English documents, a translation of the article which also we have in B/C/S, and then I have a criminal complaint which I don't have in B/C/S. Should we give separate numbers to the complaint and the article?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: So the decision from the Federal Supreme Court will be Number D25B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No, no. Sorry. Let's start in the order of appearance. The document from Slobodna Bosna, 6th June of 2002 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: -- In B/C/S would be D24B. And as we don't have any other material, only the translation of this document, or this -- yes, this clip of the paper, only this part of the English translation is admitted into evidence as D24A. I can't see where there is a basis for the admission into evidence of English translations when we don't have the underlying B/C/S text.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May we proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, just for clarification, no decision is made on the decision to conduct an investigation by the Supreme Court of BiH.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Inayat, did you at any time since June 6th, 2002, come to learn information dealing with employees of AID as those mentioned on Exhibits D24A and B?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I haven't read anything in writing. I heard this in passing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As the team leader of Team 1 involving the Stakic trial respectfully, did you do any investigation to determine whether or not the individuals who were identified as possibly having committed fraud, forgery, among other illegal criminal activities, in 1995 and 1996 were in any way related to the source from which you obtained documents as identified in lists 1 through 6?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Of these five names that are mentioned here, I've heard about this person Bakir Alispahic. I haven't heard of the other four. And let me inform this Court that Team 1 has dealt with certain persons from the AID in Bihac, Sanski Most, and also sometimes in Sarajevo, who are different persons. They are certainly not these persons here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Inayat. I didn't catch the name of the individual that you're familiar with. It didn't come out on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Mr. Bakir Alispahic. I heard this name, and I believe he had an important position in the government. But the other four, I have not heard these names before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, sir, since time that you heard of this controversy if you will with respect to individuals at AID, did you go back and run a search on the letters that were written by the OTP to the AID agency to determine whether or not there was any correspondence between these five individuals listed and those that may appear on the OTP letters? Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: First of all, I'm not aware if the OTP has been writing directly to the AID officials. I know that we forward our requests to the BiH liaison officer who attends the OTP once in a while. And through him, I believe, the requests are then forwarded in the field to the AID officials. So we don't directly deal with individuals working in the AID.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the category of documents that you obtained from various sources -- I'm sorry. I'll come back to this question. What do you mean when you say "AID officials?" What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Persons working for the agency for investigation and documentation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know, sir, what that entity was prior to 1996? What was it called?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: It was the State Security Services.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: State Security Services. Right?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, would an official in your definition of an AID official, would it be someone who worked in the capacity of the minister of internal affairs?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I think the agency for investigation and documentation is probably a different setup, it doesn't -- probably comes under the minister of interior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would your definition of an AID official be someone who worked in the capacity as assistant director of AID?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: That is possible, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would your definition of an AID official also be someone who works in the capacity of chief of AID in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I think that again is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about one as identified here possibly the same as the other capacity, as assistant director of AID? Would that also fall under your definition of AID officials?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes, anybody who is working in the agency for investigation and documentation can be referred to as an official working in that agency.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Help me with this, if you don't mind: What -- in a statement that you provided under 65 ter number 69, I think it is, on paragraph 13, you state as follows: "Evidence submitted by the federation's AID agency (on their own initiative) and documents submitted by the federation's AID agency (on requests from the Office of the Prosecutor:" And then you proceed to state as follows: "Over the years, Team 1 has received numerous documents from the AID agency which was relevant to our ongoing cases. All documents received from the AID have been submitted for evidence with the evidence unit. The documents were subsequently stamped with ERN numbers." That's paragraph 1 on page 4 of the statement -- an affidavit I guess you could call it, that you prepared. Do you remember that statement?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that statement, I don't seem to recall, having just read it, that you state that you on directive to the AID agency, that you utilised a liaison of some sort. Did the OTP, sir, at any time directly obtain from AID representatives documents utilised in the Stakic case? Again, I'm limiting it only to the 15 that you've identified on lists 1 through 6 at this time.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I think I did explain this earlier in the morning, that sometimes when investigators are visiting the field on missions, and the AID officials in the field have gathered material pursuant to a request they may have received or they have received from the liaison officer, they then sometimes request the investigator going back to The Hague to carry the documentation with them. So it is possible that the AID officials directly have submitted documents, material, to the investigators in the field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, with all these tables and the recent table we talked about briefly this morning, did you ever do an analysis to see how many documents you received from AID are in any way connected with the individuals that appear in the article in Exhibit D24A and B?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: As I told you earlier that I had heard about this particular incident in passing, and I'm looking at the names now. But I would also like to add that my team has not directly acted or interacted with these persons. There are certain persons in the AID who are deployed in Bihac or in Sanski Most. I know one in Sarajevo also, that we have had dealings with. So if you want, I can do an exercise to find out if any of the documents submitted in the Stakic case have come from these persons. But I am pretty certain that there wouldn't be any documents given to us by the individuals named in this particular document that you've given to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you don't mind, I'd like you to go through that exercise, with all due respect to the OTP and the Court, if you don't mind helping me with that. Let's look at list number 1 and go back to 65 der number 39, as you sit here now, sir -- that's that variant A and B document.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you sit here now, as the Court properly pointed out, we know when and the date that it was received on May 22nd, 1996, but we don't know from whom. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: In the case of that particular document that you're referring to, 39.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's look at another AID document, and see if you can help us from whom at the AID that document might have been received. Why don't you turn to page 3 --

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Excuse me. Can you please repeat that again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will. Sorry. On list number 1, page 3, the last entry on that page, reference 65 ter number 90, and it has an Exhibit Number I believe S21.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me by looking at this document the source, who provided this document to the OTP staff member Patrick Treanor?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Okay. Sometime in November 1995, my colleague Patrick Treanor along with other OTP staff members went to Bihac where they were shown a very, very large collection of documents that had been seized by the federation forces. And Mr. Patrick Treanor and staff with him, they identified certain material that was believed to be relevant to this -- to the investigations being conducted here. Now, in these exhibits, whether it's 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, whenever I have stated that OTP staff member Patrick Treanor received it from AID Bihac on 22/4/1996, I can tell you that an AID official working in Bihac -- I really don't know if I should be mentioning his name or not. But I have the name of the AID official who conducted the mission from April 1996 and also from November 1995, who assisted the OTP in identifying and then making copies of the material that was seized in Bihac. So I have the name, and if Your Honours would like, I can maybe pass it through the Prosecution lawyers. But I don't think I'm at liberty to mention his name here. But I have the name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the other areas, other than Bihac? Do you have that, like Sanski Most, which appears on page 1 of list number 2, 65 ter number 99? And it's Exhibit S59A and B respectfully. This was done about six months after the Bihac meeting or...

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes. I have -- Your Honours, I have on purpose not mentioned the names of AID officials. So whenever I say in my exhibit lists that OTP staff member so and so received it from the local AID office in Bihac or when I say in Sanski Most, in our records, we have the name of the person who assisted the OTP staff during the particular mission and gave the documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, help me with this, so I understand these dates a little better: How many times did they go in there, to the best of your recollection, to the various offices to obtain information prior to the indictment becoming public and prior to the December 12th, 1997, lawful search and seizure warrant that was issued?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: You mean how many field missions were conducted to meet with AID officials?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In connection with the Prijedor Municipality, correct.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I would be only guessing. I think several times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did either Patrick Treanor or other individuals involved in this mission, did they keep an inventory of all the documents that were procured relating, again, to the Prijedor Municipality?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Most definitely, and I've seen it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they keep an inventory specifically of the documents in catalogue, those documents that were obtained?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they catalogue it, make a specific inventory, indices that you provided us with Friday?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I've seen the inventories. I'm not sure it's as detailed as maybe the one that I prepared because I was given a specific task which I was given to perform. When the OTP staff went, they thought of a procedure that they wanted to adopt. But the information contained within those inventories are sufficient. I mean, they have created complete information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Can the Court cut a long story short. May we ask the witness, please, to have a look into the source of these 15 or 16 documents apparently from this list emanating from this AID, and to tell us through a representative of the OTP whether or not one of the names mentined in this article appear in these 15 or 16 documents on these lists 1 to 16, only yes or no. I don't see any relevance to fish for the names of other persons working on this issue within the AID. Is it agreeable for the Defence to proceed this way?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It would be if I can only respectfully ask the Court if they can include a search of the names of the correspondence that may have been written to the AID offices, so not just the individual who may have tendered the document to the OTP under the one scenario that Mr. Inayat has explained, but also if the OTP has written to any of these individuals from whom then possibly a directive would have been given to supply certain information. So their names may appear I believe on correspondence from the OTP to that agency. I think that would fulfill, from an investigator's standpoint, the proper chain of command [sic] of documents, how it was transferred ultimately here, if at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Mr. Inayat, has it sometimes been this way, that there was a formal request for certain documents, or was it more or less the other way around, that by chance or on a given occasion, documents especially those which are relevant for our case were given to a representative of the ICTY, without direct request for a concrete document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is, first of all, our written requests, requests for information, request for assistance, it is always addressed to the liaison officer, the liaison officer of the BiH government. We do not write directly to AID officials in the field. There have been, I believe, two liaison officers for the BiH government over the years, and we have written to them directly.
