However, it is possible that sometimes the information sought is general in nature. We may not have asked specifically for a document, but may have asked for information covering a certain aspect of our investigation. And in response to that, they may have taken the initiative and submitted documents to their liaison officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So therefore, from this it seems to be quite clear that there can be no relevance at all for outgoing letters from the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal. Relevance might be - I emphasise might be - if any document has been given to the OTP by one of the persons mentioned in this article. And I would kindly ask you just to facilitate and to settle this dispute, to find out whether or not you find one of these five names in relation to the 15 or 16 documents mentioned in lists 1 through 6 where the source is mentioned, the AID.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to restrict my response to Team 1 only. I cannot say that other teams have not written directly to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. these persons. As far as the procedures within Team 1 are concerned, we do not write directly, and we have not written directly asking for information from these five persons. We have always given our requests in writing, sometimes verbally also, to the liaison officer. However, just to make things clear and so that there is no confusion left, if I am given the 16 documents, if I am -- if somebody can point out, although I can read through the list and I can find those out myself, I can go back and do a search on these 16 documents given to us by the AID officials and to come back to the Court through the Prosecution to inform whether any of those 16 documents came to us through these five persons mentioned in the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think this exhausts the request of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I just want to point -- if I may, follow-up with one question on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Can we conclude this issue, that we request the witness to proceed this way?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Only I think I have a slightly -- if I can say modestly slightly different method that I would suggest that Mr. Inayat does it. I would suggest to him in a question that he should utilise his search databases, namely, Zybind, Keyfile and the IIF search base that he has, input the five names, and actually see on how many different occasions those names would come up with documents related. But I'll take it in any way. So we are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Actually, I think we shouldn't go into a fishing expedition. We should refrain from going into other cases. We have six lists before us. It's clearly stated where as a source AID is mentioned. And therefore, the working method should no doubt be left to the witness. Thank you. Please conclude this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please, on another point.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, with respect to the documents that were seized on December 1997 and October of 2000, at any time did the OTP seek to obtain documents out of those two searches from any military quarters or military barracks? Because you list the four locations that you seized document from in 1997, and there's no military barracks or military documents from that search and seizure. Then the same in October of 2000, you list six locations, similar to those four but I think you add the Omarska administrative building, and I think you call it the Ljubija iron mine headquarters. Did you at any time search any military office's headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: In Prijedor, we did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sir, having reviewed the indictment, namely, the fourth amended indictment, in order to determine what documents would be relevant, did you find it irrelevant the allegations in the fourth amended indictment which seemed to connect under issues of both encouragement, aiding and abetting, some sort of plan between the political bodies at that time, namely, Dr. Stakic, and the military personnel, and that's why you didn't search the military quarters?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It's not for the witness to answer such a question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, in February of 1998, actually, during your Banja Luka search and seizure, you, in fact, did search a military headquarters. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: We searched the 1st Krajina Corps headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any other military headquarters other than the 1st Krajina Corps headquarters in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: That was the one searched by our team.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So no others. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me by taking a brief look at your list 1 through 6 that you should have before you how many documents from your search of 1998 of the military headquarters in Banja Luka do you identify any documents relating to Dr. Stakic?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly slow down to the benefit of the interpreters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... We can all identify on the lists how many documents came from that seizure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sustained. If Defence counsel can point out a special document, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If you look at exhibit --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did hear the comment by the interpreters. We apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Inayat, I find on list number 6 a document that we previously discussed. From the search and seizure of 1998, it's on the last page, second to the last entry on list number 6, identified as 65 ter number 436, with a provisional number of S228 being given. My question to you, sir, is as follows: The source of that document in 1998 is not, am I correct in interpreting it, is not from the 1st Krajina military headquarters? Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a criminal investigator, can I infer, sir, that documents from the 1st Krajina military corps, since they are not included in your list 1 through 6 at this time, are not relevant against Dr. Stakic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sustained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, sir, as a criminal investigator and as the individual who conducted part of the search and seizure in 1997 how many military headquarters or offices exist in Prijedor in 1997?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: There was definitely the 43rd -- Prijedor 43rd Motorised Brigade, and also the 5th Kozara Brigade, headquarters in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you at any time, sir, receive from any other sources that you over the years have worked with, including the missions that were conducted in Bihac or Sanski Most, receive any such military documentation from either of these two military institutions, if I can call them that, namely, the 43rd Motorised Brigade and also the 5th Kozara Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes. We have received documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me from what source?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: These mainly came from two sources. I can get you the facts as to how many documents were given and by whom. But I believe that the searches that were undertaken by the OTP in Bihac, some material came from that particular collection. And later on, when OTP staff members visited Sanski Most, I think in 1997 -- 1996 and 1997, Ms. Jutta Paczulla, I believe her searches also resulted in receiving documents regarding the military headquarters that I just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, just that so I'm clear and I know we passed this point, those are documents in Bihac and Sanski Most that were obtained during a mission involving AID. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes. These are documents which in 1995 it was the State Security Service, but later in 1996 it became the AID. So they assisted us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the Court's permission, if the usher can show Mr. Inayat Exhibit S68 and S69. You tell me, sir, when you've had a chance to look at that document, and then I'll proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And if I can just for the Court, for the record, just clarify that those documents appear on list number 2 of Mr. Inayat's report, specifically page 2, and they are the second and third entry on page 2 of list 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you had a chance to review those documents, sir?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I've looked at these two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at page 2, list 2, and looking at the source of the information that you identify these documents with, these are documents which purport to have the signature of Dr. Milomir Stakic. These documents were subject to some forensic analysis, if you will, and I understand from our earlier discussions today, you're unaware of that. But just so the record is clear, these are some of those documents we referenced earlier. Can you tell me, sir, from who the individual is that gave the OTP staff member Pat Treanor these documents?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think we have settled this.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You're right, Your Honour. I can ask another question to follow this up, if I may. Thank you for reminding me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we tell, Mr. Inayat, from those two documents or do you know when dealing with issues of chain of custody and inventorying certain documents, do you know how is it that another municipality such as Bihac or Sanski Most, how is it and why is it would they be in possession of documents from a municipality such as Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Starting from September going on until October of 1995, when the federation forces reoccupied or captured Bihac, Klupa, and Sanski Most, Kljuc, according to the information given to us by the local authorities is that all documents that had been left there in the military headquarters of these municipalities or the police headquarters or the courts or the Municipal Assembly building or the police station, they were collected from those locations in those municipalities, and they were brought and centralised in Bihac. That is when most of the documents even belonging to Prijedor were recovered from these municipalities and put in Bihac. That is where in November 1995 the OTP staff when they learned of this large collection, they went and they viewed the material. So it was in Bihac that the whole collection had been assembled for us to review it. Because in those initial days as some of us may recall, it wasn't very easy travelling to the region. So Bihac was a central point, and that's where most of the documents were kept for our review.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just trying to understand, and help me with this: If we're talking about Prijedor, and I understand documents may be related to the municipalities of Sanski Most, Kljuc, Krupa, and Petrovac. But tell me: Why would documents from the Prijedor Municipality that had not been taken over by as you call them the federation forces, how is it that those documents from Prijedor would find their way in any of these other municipalities and ultimately in Bihac? By simply looking at those two documents, wouldn't you agree with me that they are not addressed to any entity within those municipalities that we mention?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I agree with you that these two documents have been created in Prijedor by the local authorities there. But as to the question how they made their way to Bihac, I'm afraid I can't answer that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't want to split hairs here, I'm not making any assessment as to where the documents were created, sir, with all due respect. My question to you is: When you're determining issues of chain of custody and when you are creating this IIF form and trying to determine how to inventory documents such -- and believe me this is a sample of the documents that you present to us, sir -- how did those documents, did you ever ask the individuals in Bihac or Sanski Most or any representative from AID how is it that they have documents relating to a completely different municipality, namely, Prijedor, since on the face of those documents certainly one can see it was not directed to anyone in any of those municipalities, and it certainly was not carbon copied to any of those such individuals?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: The one thing that investigators should have taken into account, which I can see from these two documents that they have, that they have -- before receiving these copies, photocopies, they have certified that they have compared it with the original. So they have seen the original there. Now, as to your question whether the investigators at that point asked the local authorities as to how they got the document, we have statements given by the local authorities. I know of one particular statement. I believe the answer to your question probably could be in that statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Although I'd like to ask you for that, maybe I should direct it to the Court. If you would be kind enough to prepare it, and we'll ask the Court if we can have that statement. And then at the Court's direction or the OTP's trial counsel's direction, we may or may not receive it. Let me ask you this: Those two documents seem to indicate to you that originals are in existence. So if it's an original signature that appears that purports to have Dr. Milomir Stakic's name on it, it would be likely that a forensic expert - which hopefully we're going to hear from - would find that signature to be greater than probable to match that of Dr. Milomir Stakic. True or false?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Not relevant for this witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, sir, in your -- both your initial attempt to try to determine whether Rule 68 was complied with and verified that the documents -- that the Defence was receiving pursuant to that rule, is it your practice to limit that review and overview to the documents that were lawfully seized, namely, that from December 12th, 1997, or did you also, sir, include, pursuant to Rule 68, all the documents including those from Banja Luka and those in your possession from the AID agencies?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: The Rule 68 searches are -- have been or are being done for all documentation, whether these are witness statements, whether these are seized documents, whether they are documents given to us by the AID officials. So it's across the board.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If the usher would be kind enough to show Mr. Inayat Exhibit S75, which appears on page 3 of list number 2, the first entry. And perhaps while the usher is standing there, he may remove the other documents before the witness to reduce any confusion that might occur.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you had an opportunity to review that document, sir?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now with respect to this S75, do you know if an original exists in Bihac or in any other place?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I ask that the word "original" be further clarified. I understand, I think, what counsel means by original, but I think the witness is using -- I want to be clear whether we're talking about an original in the sense that the OTP took a copy of whatever was in Bihac, and that itself may or may not have been an original, would have been a copy, as opposed to an original with the original signature because these are two different uses of the word.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm using the common definition of the word "original." If I misunderstood Mr. Inayat in that there may be two originals or two different definitions of the word "original," perhaps he can explain it to me. But quite frankly, my request was based on - and my questioning Mr. Inayat was based on your follow-up answer identifying documents in the possession of various entities in Bihac or wherever, that they were deemed to be originals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe I should have asked you to define it, so I apologise to you. But what do you mean when you say "original"?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I would tend to think that what was with the Bihac office were originals. The reason -- what I'm basing this on is that if you --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under which definition, though?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I'll come to that. Because if you read the comments by Mr. Treanor on the certified copy, he very clearly says that I, Patrick J. Treanor confirm that I have compared this copy with the original and hereby certify that this copy is a true and accurate reproduction of the original. If Mr. Treanor was merely photocopying a photocopy, then probably that, too, would have been mentioned. However, I also take Mr. Koumjian's point, and I can go back to Mr. Treanor and then confirm this with him, that when he says original here, does he mean the actual original or that some originals can also have many copies. Could it be a copy of an original? So that is something I can check with Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But what you just read about Mr. Treanor is not something he actually wrote. It's a stamp used by the OTP and merely placed on the document. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: He wouldn't do such a thing without knowing what he's doing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not debating that. What you read that you claim Mr. Treanor wrote down is actually just a stamp used by the OTP. He didn't write that in his own words, did he?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a stamp. All he did was sign it and probably date it. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: He signed it and dated, it yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think I understand what an original copy or copy of an original is, but bear with me on this definition because I may not get it right. If someone makes a copy of an original, of an original document, let's say my notes here, if you copy that, what is it? An original or a copy?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: It would become a photocopy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If a third person copies the copy, would it be a copy of a copy or would it be an original, or a copy of an original?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: If a third person was to photocopy, it would become a photocopy of a photocopy of the original.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All the documents that the OTP has presented which bear the signature of Dr. Milomir Stakic, specifically those identified in list numbers 1 through 6 that you have before you, are you telling us, sir, since the stamp that appears on that document by Mr. Patrick Treanor clearly is that someone has possession of the original documents bearing Dr. Stakic's signature? Is that what you believe?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: The original has to be somewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sir, you believe that the original is still in the possession of persons in Bihac. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I'm not saying that. I need to check that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me show you a document that, I think, you received from the AID offices, and that would be Exhibit S88A and B. 65 ter number 305.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If the Court would allow the usher to present that to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please do so. List number?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Again -- thank you, Your Honour. It's on list number 2, page 4, I believe. Yes, we're dealing with that document, list number 2, page 4. If I may, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly slow down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Inayat, just let me know when you've had a chance to look at the document. I'd like to ask you if that stamp that you referred to in the prior two documents bearing Dr. Stakic's name from materials that were received from the AID in Bihac, whether this exhibit, 88, which according to your list 2 sourcing information was received from the AID office in Sanski Most on November 9th, 2001, by yourself. Does that indicate, sir, whether you received an original or a copy or any form of definition of original or copy that you'd like to use?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Most probably I received --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, what does it -- I apologise for interrupting. What does it say on the document, original or copy?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: You mean on the source?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, on the document itself. Exhibit 88. Is there a stamp on it at all?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I don't see anything here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you went back to do this source to fill out that document, how did you learn that it was a document that you actually received on November 9th, 2001, from the offices of AID in Sanski Most? How do you know that? It's not on the document, is it?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: By looking at the ERN number and then doing a search on the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then from there you would look at the registration index, and then find the IIF. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But from this document, we are unable to determine whether or not you obtained the original or a copy. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: From this document? Yes, it's not possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just so I know the protocol and procedure that your team may have used, from other documents which may bear the signature of Dr. Milomir Stakic which do not have the stamp as the stamp revealed that you testified in connection with Mr. Patrick Treanor, should we assume that an original exists, that it was a copy of a copy, or should we make no assumptions at all in connection with the authenticity and reliability of those documents?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: If the document has been provided by a witness or the local authorities and it's an original, that would be mentioned in the IIF form. And wherever it's possible for an investigator to look at the original which cannot be given to us by the source, but we are allowed to keep a copy, we can certify that. That after having compared this copy with the original, we are taking into evidence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does Team 1 also keep track of a diary or inventory of the times that you would make contact with the witnesses that would be called before the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes, we would do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For example, if we go back to the individual we mentioned earlier this morning, Mr. Edward Sebastian Vulliamy, there would be some way through these search bases Zybind and Keyfind that we can determine, A, how many people made contact with Mr. Vulliamy; B, how and where they made contact with Mr. Vulliamy; and C, whether or not there was any correspondence between the OTP and that particular witness. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: If it's a question of correspondence, then it can be found from the very early years also. But as far as making entries of telephone contacts are concerned, we only started doing this I think sometime in 1999.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about with respect to meetings that members of the trial team or the team comprised of Team Number 1, would there be any inventory to tell us where and with whom individuals of Team Number 1 meet with this witness Vulliamy?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: If the meetings with Mr. Vulliamy or any other witness for that matter had taken place after 1999, the person from the Office of the Prosecutor is supposed to record that information in a particular database that we have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But before 1999, there would be no such documentation. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Individuals, investigators and lawyers may have kept those records.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know in connection with witness Vulliamy whether or not any such records exist with respect to the meetings he may have had with the OTP prior to the indictment becoming public and before his, what I coin neutrally, illegal interview with accused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, first, the characterisation of an interview as illegal is something for the Court to make and not for counsel. We don't believe any illegal interview took place. All this regarding Mr. Vulliamy I believe was covered by Mr. Ostojic in his cross-examination of Mr. Vulliamy in the Kovacevic case. There's no dispute that Mr. Vulliamy met with members of the Office of the Prosecutor. Apparently, there's some issue, and I don't claim to be completely aware of all that was said because I haven't finished reading all that transcript. I think it's a thousand pages long. There's apparently some dispute about what or at least counsel has some allegations regarding what may have been told to Mr. Vulliamy before he spoke to the accused in, I believe, 1996. But I don't see that these questions about how records are kept of interviews with a witness would be helpful in that since all parties agree that there was a meeting between Mr. Vulliamy and members of the Office of the Prosecutor. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think we are all eager to know this from Mr. Vulliamy in person. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm sure we will. But I think that we have an opportunity with the criminal investigator here who can tell us at least what the policy may have been in connection with meeting with witnesses prior to extracting information from them. And I think Mr. Inayat has answered that in part, and I'm just trying to determine whether or not any of those records exist so that we can be thorough when we do question him. But I didn't limit my questioning of Mr. Inayat specifically to Mr. Vulliamy. As a practical matter, and I was hoping as a courtesy to Mr. Inayat, I was trying to just reference a witness by way of example. There were other witnesses that we contend, Your Honour, have been interviewed prior to the interviews that were conducted by the OTP which were, again, based upon information and belief, a burden which we gladly accept we will meet interviewed by representatives of AID and then ultimately have been converted into OTP witnesses for whatever reason. So our questioning, with all due respect, is a little broader than just Mr. Vulliamy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The rejected question was limited to Mr. Vulliamy only.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Generally speaking, Mr. Inayat, the witnesses that meet with the OTP after 1999, it's my understanding that those meetings and interviews are specifically identified, logged, diaried, and inventoried, or any such word. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to 1999, any such interviews conducted with witnesses by either Team Number 1, the trial team included, of course, under that category, records may exist of contact between Team Number 1 and witnesses; you just don't know. And it was basically not a policy but it was done on an individual level, correct, or practice?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Before 1999, as I said, we didn't have the database which we are using now to indicate each and every contact that we make with witnesses. Prior to that, persons within the team, if they were making any contacts, they may have kept their personal records indicating what the contact was about, the date when the contact was made, and the substance of the conversation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a couple more questions, if I may, sir. Was there ever a request made to the Tribunal to search and seize documents pursuant to a lawful warrant from the location involving the military headquarters the 5th Kozara Brigade and the 43 Motorised Brigade that you identified earlier? Has any such request been made, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: At the time of --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I object. The relevance of whether a request was made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: If the Defence could explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The fourth amended indictment clearly makes allegations between a political figure and political figures relating to the military. I think it's relevant not only to determine whether or not a Rule 38 directive was issued by the Prosecutor herself to seize those documents, or whether or not at any time the OTP thought that it would be relevant since it's highlighted in numerous paragraphs in their indictment, whether they would ask leave for a proper warrant to search and seize documents within an entity that they tried to make a nexus with our client, the accused Dr. Stakic. Did they make even an effort is really what we're trying to determine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The witness may answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, as far as searches of the military installations in Prijedor is concerned, they weren't considered in December 1997. But I know that in later years, I've also been involved in some discussions that we ought to have done that. But I believe, because I wasn't on the team at the time, there were limited resources, and probably going to a couple of additional locations could have caused logistical problems. So that could have been the reason for not having searched those premises. But your question, we haven't made any written efforts so far. But I know that we had wanted to search those locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May the usher show the witness S232, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please, if you can give us the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It doesn't appear actually on the list 1 through 6. It's a separate exhibit that was identified and admitted into evidence by another witness. I believe it's relevant to Mr. Inayat's testimony, specifically because it references the information index form that we talked about briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I please first have a look on this document so that I know what it's all about.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Just for the record, it's a confidential exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sorry. Okay. I didn't note that, Your Honour. So I apologise if we've identified it. So we would ask the Court to redact the portions wherein I identified the document by its heading. Because it's confidential, I guess I wasn't supposed to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I don't think you mentioned anything about the contents of this document --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I don't think anything has to be redacted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I feel better already. May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Except perhaps the entire cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: If it's the last thing for today, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With respect to this Exhibit S232, sir, can you tell us -- do you know, sir, under the category that's identified on the left centre of that page with the question mark and the answer "no" -- do you see that? It's the second line in the centre of that document.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me what that means?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Just to be sure, are you talking of chain of custody?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Because it says "no" several times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's a document you're familiar with, right, as the team leader of Team 1? Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's preprinted, the information that they are seeking to obtain from people who obtain documents, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: In my opinion, it should have been yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why is that?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: These are documents seized by the investigator which were in the possession of a person. Then for purposes of, you know, chain of custody, it should be, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the next section of that same line? If you keep going to the right, and that section after the area we're just discussing, it also has another "no" after the question. And I hesitate to identify it because it's somewhat confidential. But in any event, it asks whether or not something has been signed. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: If the document that was received by the investigator, if it was signed, then it should have said yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's your document. I just want to understand it, because I have trouble understanding some of these documents from time to time. Does that document that you utilise on a regular basis on Team Number 1 for this trial relating to Stakic, is that a similiar-type document that you use for all the documents from whether it's AID or whether it's from documents seized in Prijedor, Banja Luka, or from any other entity? This is the type of form you're utilising. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: This is the information index form that we use whenever we receive material from witnesses or from any other sources.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the question on that centre paragraph when it says "signed," it's asking the question of the person who obtained the documents, whether or not the documents that were seized, regardless of whether or not it was a proper seizure or confiscation of document, it's simply inquiring - and you correct me if I am wrong - are the documents, sir, that you obtained from the accused in this particular case, were they signed by the accused or were they blank? Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I believe I've already answered that. If the documents that were seized by the investigator, if they had been signed, if those were signed documents, this particular field should have been said "yes."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from this, if you as the team leader had reviewed the IIF forms which we're asking you to do, by the way, for other documents, if you were to review this IIF form, and if I asked you, sir, with respect to the documents identified on Exhibit 232, were those documents signed by Dr. Milomir Stakic or were they unsigned? Based upon that exhibit and the information that you have, what would your opinion be?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: If I look at this IIF form, it says no. And if I look at the original document and it's signed, I know there's something wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, that's all we have, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I recall that the parties wanted to discuss the admission of Document S160 in the presence of Mr. Inayat?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If I can just have a moment. Thank you, Your Honour. Does the witness have the exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I don't think so. You have it just in your hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. May the usher then be kind enough to give the exhibit to the witness. And if I can have a moment to just ask him a couple questions on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please, for my own and all our recollection have a look on this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We interrupt the proceedings for some minutes, if I understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I'll wait.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May we please hear once again the objections by the Defence to this document tendered by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In addition to the objections that we outlined to the Court initially when the OTP tried to produce this document, we find at least from our cursory review of list numbers 1 through 6 that the document does not appear to have any items necessary or factors to be considered for purposes of authenticity. I don't believe the document appears, and I'm just saying it somewhat cautiously based upon a cursory review, within the documents listed by Mr. Inayat on lists 1 through 6. And quite frankly, Your Honour, because I don't have the specific document in front of me, and my apologies to the Court and the witness for that, I would like, if necessary, to add specifically some other objections that we've consistently maintained with respect to these documents. In light of the time, perhaps if the OTP is going to have further questions and possibly the Court, if it would be prudent and efficient to proceed with this particular document and further our response or bases of our objection for tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I would appreciate if you could finalise the testimony of Mr. Inayat today. Are there a number of additional questions by the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I have some.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Limited to how many minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I think ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. Then let's do this today. But let's -- I think there was a request for an interruption of about five minutes. Let's do so. If the Defence could be so kind and collect the arguments opposed to this Document 160 so we can decide on the admission apparently in the absence of Witness Inayat because this document is not reflected in lists 1 to 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If we can -- the usher is not here, Your Honour, so with your permission --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It's no problem. The Court becomes more and more normal, from my point of view. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Are we permitted to examine the document? Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Can we in the meantime hear from the OTP, please, what is envisaged for tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Tomorrow Mr. Sebire, the person who has compiled the exhumation evidence, is prepared to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And you want us to read this some hundred pages until tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: It's actually I believe 52 or 54 pages of text, and the rest is an annex.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: All participants are in possession of these documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: They had the document on Friday, and the translation today.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We have, Your Honour. We received it last week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. We can proceed this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: The handwriting report is being translated and is not yet -- it has not yet been done. Also, Your Honour asked for several -- for some kind of help in interpreting, which I understand, that report because of the numbers used, or ERN numbers. The witness is available on Wednesday, but it's going to be rather difficult to have that done by then. I have to meet with that witness, I hope, sometime -- I'll be calling Mr. Sebire tomorrow, so it's going to be difficult. We could try to call him on Wednesday. I would ask that we at least start a little bit later on Wednesday so I can meet with him before we start. I can try, but I can't promise to get something more helpful to the Court regarding the numbers that the report uses. I've asked -- I don't know if we have an answer yet, whether we could get an electronic copy of that report so we could put in the numbers, but I have not yet received an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This would be excellent, but no doubt priority has the availability of this expert already on Monday -- sorry, on Wednesday. So let's come to the famous document S160.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: As the document depicts on its face, it's from the SDS municipal board. We believe that it does not meet the necessary guidelines and procedures permitted for documents that are not authenticated; namely, the signature, the dating, to whom it may have been addressed to. However, that document, as far as the Defence is concerned, may be subsequently used by either experts or other individuals who may be analysing the materials relating to Prijedor Municipality because there might be within this document some so-called exculpatory materials. So we would like before we can specifically outline whether there's any probative value to this document, that we would need to find the sourcing information of the document, in particular. And then we independent, as we have with most other documents, will attempt to do to do some verification with respect to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So following the -- this was mentioned already once today I recall, the liberal policy on the admission of evidence, this document is admitted into evidence as S160A and B correspondingly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may just tender the document back to the usher, I think it's the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would the usher please take the document and hand it over to the registry once again. And please, then, in a very concentrated way because we are already out of time, the remaining questions by the OTP. Thank you. Re-examined by Mr. Koumjian:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very quickly, Mr. Inayat, you were asked regarding documents that the OTP received from Bihac. Is it correct that Bihac was simply the location point where these documents were brought by AID and stored, not necessarily the location where they were seized? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: In their offices, there was a place where they gathered all the material.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, Bihac itself never fell to the VRS or Serbian forces during the war, unlike places like Sanski Most and Kljuc, which are adjoining municipalities to Prijedor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Inayat, I'm going to ask you a question regarding military matters. And if you are not familiar please do not -- if you don't know the answer, please indicate and do not guess. Do you know if in the municipalities of Sanski Most or Kljuc or other areas that fell in 1995 to the opposing forces, those forces opposing the SDS or Serbian forces, whether or not the military units from Prijedor, such as the 43 Motorised Brigade and the Kozara Light Brigade, were in those municipalities that fell to federation forces in 1995?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We would object, Your Honour, to relevance. We think that it is relevant that the criminal investigators did not obtain a warrant or, pursuant to Rule 38, Prosecutor's directive, to seize documents relating to the Prijedor Municipality. Relating to municipalities such as Sanski Most, Kljuc, Krupa, and Petrovac, it's totally relevant to our case, as the Court has previously ruled when the OTP tried to obtain information from the Sanski Most municipality specifically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think the question was put in a very careful way. And only if you really can give a responsible answer, please do so. If not, refrain.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm -- I would rather refrain from answering this question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because you're not certain?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Because I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Inayat, regarding the events of 1995, are you familiar with the fact that, in fact, Sanski Most and Kljuc, for example, did fall to federation forces that year?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: In September and October of 1995, these two municipalities fell, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar, from speaking to witnesses and persons from the area, that the retreat of Serbian forces at that time was a very -- it was a sudden fall? It was a chaotic retreat of Serbian forces, that they went back to Prijedor, and in fact Arkan in Prijedor punished some of the forces from Sanski Most and had them shave their heads for cowardice?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: I'm not certain about the Arkan incident, but I know from the witnesses that I've spoken to and statements that I've taken and other documentary evidence that I've seen, that the retreat from Sanski Most, Kljuc, and other municipalities that fell was a hasty one and a chaotic one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find in your searches of various locations in Prijedor and in Banja Luka and other locations that the same document could appear in multiple locations, and that each location had a copy of the document?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: That has happened, yes. And I can confirm this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going quickly to the IIF form that you were shown, was that form created by Mr. O'Donnell?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: It appears that it was prepared by him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your understanding, is it correct, that the items in the IIF form are not originals, that they were photocopies of the items that were taken from Mr. Stakic, that those were the items placed into evidence, not the originals? And when I use the word "original" now, I'm sorry, because I asked for a definition before, I do not mean these are necessarily the first time a document was produced. It could be a photocopy. But the items, by "original," I mean the items in the possession of Dr. Stakic.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: My understanding is that - and I could be wrong; I would have to go back to verify this - that whatever Mr. Stakic had on his person, Mr. O'Donnell took it and IIFed it. But I could be wrong.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, Mr. Inayat, didn't you just testify this morning you returned those items, the originals - again, I'm using the word in the sense of what was taken from Mr. Stakic - to the Detention Unit, and they are not in evidence?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes. The things that were returned, they were never IIFed. For example, personal things like license, driver's license, I believe, or other car documents, they were never seized or IIFed. Those were returned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be corrected that the person who would know exactly what was IIFed and ERNed would be Mr. O'Donnell?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I can't see any further questions. The trial stays adjourned until tomorrow morning, 9.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
